Providing these supplies and management protocols in La Guaira and Miranda should be an early priority. Finally, given that more than half of the pharmacies, gynecology clinics, and immunization areas show visible damage to their walls, these interventions should be accompanied by minor infrastructure repairs and the installation of access ramps at the five facilities that do not yet have them. Water, Sanitation, and Hygiene (WASH) Recommendations The rehabilitation of handwashing stations should be the top priority for this component: with only 24.8% operational — the lowest rate among all evaluated water points — and nearly two-thirds lacking soap, this is also the intervention with the greatest potential for immediate impact on disease prevention, starting with the two facilities that reported 0% operational stations. At the same time, it is necessary to provide testing kits and train staff so that water quality monitoring — currently practiced in less than half of the facilities — becomes a routine practice and so that staff establish a maintenance schedule for storage tanks, more than a third of which currently fail to meet basic functionality criteria.

At the same time, it is necessary to provide testing kits and train staff so that water quality monitoring — currently practiced in less than half of the facilities — becomes a routine practice and so that staff establish a maintenance schedule for storage tanks, more than a third of which currently fail to meet basic functionality criteria. The management of medical waste represents another gap that requires attention, in coordination with municipal authorities or service providers. One-third of facilities have not had biohazardous waste collected in over a year and up to 44% of facilities have not had sharps waste collected in over a year. Furthermore, since only 22.2% of the centers have an established infection prevention and control committee, it is advisable to take advantage of these infrastructure interventions to reactivate such committees and expand staff training on cleaning and disinfection protocols.

Furthermore, since only 22.2% of the centers have an established infection prevention and control committee, it is advisable to take advantage of these infrastructure interventions to reactivate such committees and expand staff training on cleaning and disinfection protocols. Community Protection and Psychosocial Support Recommendations A recurring finding in this component is the gap between what communities know and what they can actually access: most participants know where to turn in the event of violence or a mental health issue, but very few are aware of specific community support groups. Closing this gap requires mapping and actively publicizing existing resources, as well as strengthening or creating support groups in communities where none exist. The perception of insecurity in community spaces — shared by 2 in 3 participants — along with reports of insufficient child supervision, points to the need to establish safe spaces and structured activities for children and adolescents, prioritizing areas where the perception of risk is highest.

chunks.text: Closing this gap requires mapping and actively publicizing existing resources, as well as strengthening or creating support groups in communities where none exist. The perception of insecurity in community spaces — shared by 2 in 3 participants — along with reports of insufficient child supervision, points to the need to establish safe spaces and structured activities for children and adolescents, prioritizing areas where the perception of risk is highest. Regarding parenting practices, the fact that most households already practice or combine forms of respectful parenting provides a favorable foundation on which to build awareness-raising sessions aimed at reducing the use of punishment, which is still present in 14% of households. Needs Assessment Report: Venezuela – July 2026 Page 14 of 15 Finally, although family separation and the absence of adult care are not predominant phenomena, their presence in a significant proportion of communities justifies training community and healthcare actors in both early identification and referral. The findings of this report reveal a pattern common to all three sectors evaluated: there is knowledge and existing capacity within communities and health facilities, but there is a lack of supplies, infrastructure, and the access mechanisms needed to translate that knowledge into effective practice.

chunks.text: Needs Assessment Report: Venezuela – July 2026 Page 14 of 15 Finally, although family separation and the absence of adult care are not predominant phenomena, their presence in a significant proportion of communities justifies training community and healthcare actors in both early identification and referral. The findings of this report reveal a pattern common to all three sectors evaluated: there is knowledge and existing capacity within communities and health facilities, but there is a lack of supplies, infrastructure, and the access mechanisms needed to translate that knowledge into effective practice. For example, communities know how to prevent dengue, but breeding sites persist; and health personnel know how to manage pregnancy complications, but the medications needed to do so are lacking. Therefore, the most effective response will not be one that treats health, WASH, and protection as separate components, but rather one that takes an integrated approach to addressing the practical barriers that prevent the application of existing knowledge and prioritizes the facilities and communities where gaps across multiple sectors are concentrated simultaneously. chunks.title: Situation Report No.8: Earthquakes in Venezuela 2026 (M7.2 and M7.5), 30 July 2026
chunks.text: **HIGHLIGHTS** More than a month after the two earthquakes struck north-central Venezuela on 24 June 2026, the emergency response remains active while laying the groundwork for early recovery. Priorities now center on sustaining essential health services, strengthening referral pathways, and supporting temporary camps, while preventing public health risks and ensuring the continuous, needs-based supply of medicines and essential equipment. Integrated surveillance continues to strengthen early detection and public health risk monitoring across affected areas. Approximately 30,638 vaccine doses have been administered, while laboratory, environmental and event-based surveillance activities continue supporting timely verification and response.

chunks.title: Situation Report No.8: Earthquakes in Venezuela 2026 (M7.2 and M7.5), 30 July 2026
chunks.text: Integrated surveillance continues to strengthen early detection and public health risk monitoring across affected areas. Approximately 30,638 vaccine doses have been administered, while laboratory, environmental and event-based surveillance activities continue supporting timely verification and response. Transitional camps now shelter 24,477 people across 107 sites at 87% occupancy, with health, WASH, and protection needs extending beyond La Guaira toward Distrito Capital and Miranda as populations move, requiring coordinated action across multiple states. PAHO/WHO continued supporting the response with critical medicines and equipment, benefiting 29 actors through its supplies and donations to date, and facilitated logistical support for 11 accepted donor offers. The latest delivery equipped four health facilities in La Guaira—extending primary care to 40,000 people—and delivered WASH items ensuring safe water for 800 families and nearly 110,000 people per month.

SITUATION ANALYSIS Continuity of essential health services One month after the earthquakes, the health response is increasingly transitioning from emergency service delivery towards early recovery and longer-term health system strengthening. Current priorities focus on restoring the functionality of health service networks, maintaining referral pathways, addressing priority infrastructure and equipment gaps, and ensuring continuity of essential and specialized care. During the reporting period, PAHO/WHO completed the assessment of the nine Community Integrated Health Areas (ASICs) in La Guaira and supported prioritization of actions across the health service network to guide the allocation of emergency resources. The assessment provided a clearer understanding of service availability, operational needs and coordination between health facilities and transitional camps, while strengthening technical support for health network management.

chunks.text: During the reporting period, PAHO/WHO completed the assessment of the nine Community Integrated Health Areas (ASICs) in La Guaira and supported prioritization of actions across the health service network to guide the allocation of emergency resources. The assessment provided a clearer understanding of service availability, operational needs and coordination between health facilities and transitional camps, while strengthening technical support for health network management. Hospital functionality Operational assessments continue informing prioritization of recovery interventions across affected health facilities. Current planning includes infrastructure rehabilitation in eight prioritized facilities: three hospitals and one outpatient facility in La Guaira, three hospitals in Distrito Capital and one hospital in Miranda. A detailed operational assessment of 20 health facilities across La Guaira, Miranda and Distrito Capital identified significant variations in service functionality and persistent gaps affecting diagnostic capacity, specialized services and health workforce availability.

Washington, D.C.: PAHO/WHO; 2026. | © PAHO/WHO, 2026 Earthquake in Venezuela Situation Report N.8 Health service delivery Health service delivery continues to evolve from the management of acute earthquake-related trauma towards comprehensive essential care and recovery-oriented services. Current priorities include maintaining access to primary health care, strengthening continuity of care for people living with chronic conditions, supporting specialized services and improving coordination between health facilities, referral networks and transitional camps. Noncommunicable diseases continue to represent an important component of health service demand, particularly hypertension and diabetes. During the reporting period, national authorities and partners advanced the development of standardized tools and digital systems to improve identification and follow-up of people living with noncommunicable diseases, while technical discussions continued to harmonize clinical pathways and referral processes.

During the reporting period, national authorities and partners advanced the development of standardized tools and digital systems to improve identification and follow-up of people living with noncommunicable diseases, while technical discussions continued to harmonize clinical pathways and referral processes. Emergency Medical Teams (EMTs) The international EMT response is progressively transitioning from surge deployment toward sustained support for national health services and early recovery. As of 29 July, ten EMTs remained operational, concentrated in La Guaira, Caracas, and Miranda, with specialized capacities in maternal, newborn and child health, clinical rehabilitation, and remote clinical support. As of the reporting period, EMTs had submitted 290 Minimum Data Set (MDS) reports documenting 28,827 consultations, including 594 hospital admissions, 241 major surgical procedures, 253 minor surgical procedures and 1,814 occupied bed-days.

chunks.text: National authorities are conducting assessments to identify people requiring continued rehabilitation following surgical management of trauma-related conditions and to facilitate their integration into the health system. During the reporting period, a rehabilitation strengthening project was developed for La Guaira, Distrito Capital, Miranda and Aragua. The proposed intervention aims to strengthen rehabilitation services across the four prioritized states and support three specialized rehabilitation referral centres through the provision of essential equipment and supplies. Health facility recovery planning also continues to address priority gaps in infrastructure, water and sanitation, diagnostic capacity, medical supplies and health information systems. Identified needs include laboratory reagents, diagnostic equipment, medicines for chronic diseases, pediatric formulations, mental health kits and medical and surgical supplies.

Mental Health and Psychosocial Support (MHPSS) Implementation of the MPPS National Mental Health Response Plan continues, with Mental Health Points serving as an operational mechanism to coordinate psychosocial support and referral pathways for populations living in transitional camps. Technical coordination and implementation activities continue across Distrito Capital, Miranda and La Guaira, supported by specialized mental health personnel and collaboration with national and international partners. Current priorities include strengthening the integration of mental health and psychosocial support within primary health care, consolidating referral pathways, expanding communitybased services and ensuring access to specialized care for people with more complex mental health needs.

PAHO/WHO RESPONSE PAHO/WHO continues to support the response with critically needed medical supplies and medicines, having shipped 32 metric tons (MT) to Venezuela to date. These supplies have been and are being distributed locally based on each health facility's service profile, the medical needs of shelters, and specific requirements to strengthen response capacities, ensuring maximum impact (see Annex 2 and Annex 3). The latest distribution of supplies included four IEHK (Interagency Emergency Health Kit) Supplementary Equipment Unit, delivered and installed across four health facilities: the Caraballeda Outpatient Clinic, the Naiguatá Specialized Outpatient Clinic, the Guaracarumbo CDI, and the Balneario CDI. Together, these supplies provide primary health care coverage for a total of 40,000 people, distributed across the communities of Caraballeda (covering ~23% of its population), Naiguatá (~50%), ASIC Guaracarumbo (~25%), and Catia La Mar (~14.28%).

chunks.text: The latest distribution of supplies included four IEHK (Interagency Emergency Health Kit) Supplementary Equipment Unit, delivered and installed across four health facilities: the Caraballeda Outpatient Clinic, the Naiguatá Specialized Outpatient Clinic, the Guaracarumbo CDI, and the Balneario CDI. Together, these supplies provide primary health care coverage for a total of 40,000 people, distributed across the communities of Caraballeda (covering ~23% of its population), Naiguatá (~50%), ASIC Guaracarumbo (~25%), and Catia La Mar (~14.28%). As part of the Water, Sanitation and Hygiene (WASH) response, a direct delivery to the Punta Gorda Desalination Plant included 800 jerry cans for safe household water storage, along with water purification tablets. The jerry cans directly benefit 800 families (between 3,200 and 4,000 people), with one allocated per household, while the purification tablets ensure safe drinking water for 109,899 people per month. PAHO/WHO also strengthened Venezuela's epidemiological surveillance capacities through the delivery of molecular diagnostic supplies.

The package included 16 types of reagents for the molecular and serological diagnosis of 14 priority diseases and public health events, helping sustain and expand national technical capacity. Diagnostics reinforced cover vector-borne diseases (dengue, chikungunya, Zika, Oropouche, yellow fever, equine encephalitis, and West Nile virus), respiratory pathogens (COVID-19, influenza, avian influenza, respiratory syncytial virus, and human metapneumovirus), and zoonoses and other public health priorities, including hantavirus and leptospirosis. PAHO/WHO continues providing technical and logistical support to facilitate in-kind donations from international partners and neighboring countries.

chunks.title: PAHO Regional Situation Report No.8: Measles in the Region of the Americas (31 July 2026)
chunks.text: **Situation Overview** Between epidemiological week (EW) 1 and EW 29 of 2026 (ending on 25 July 2026), the Region of the Americas reported 47,026 confirmed measles cases from 17 countries and territories, representing approximately a 5-fold increase compared to the same period in 2025. Guatemala (30,040), Mexico (12,233), the United States (2,318) and Canada (1,107) accounted for the majority (97%) of confirmed cases. Additionally, 48 deaths have been reported. The increase in the regional cumulative total compared with Situation Report No.7 is primarily attributable to Guatemala, which remains the major contributor of newly confirmed cases with 1395 added cases, followed by additional cases reported by Mexico with 119 added cases, Peru with 93 added cases, the United States with 77 added cases, Canada with 9 added cases, Bolivia with 3 added cases and Colombia with 1 added case.

During EW 27 and EW 28 of 2026, the Region of the Americas reported 1,697 new confirmed measles cases across seven countries and territories, representing a 6.7% decrease compared with the previous two-week period (EW 25-26; 1,818 new cases)2 (Figure 1). The decrease was driven mainly by fewer cases reported in Guatemala after the retrospective update was incorporated in the previous situation report. Following the earthquakes, while the risk of measles introduction and spread in Venezuela remains a concern, there have been no confirmed cases reported in the country thus far.

chunks.title: PAHO Regional Situation Report No.8: Measles in the Region of the Americas (31 July 2026)
chunks.text: Washington, D.C.: PAHO/WHO; 2026. | © PAHO/WHO, 2026 PAHO Response by Strategic Pillar (5) 3 Coordination PAHO has finalized a Strategic Response Plan for the regional measles outbreak, developed by the IMST into a donor-ready Appeal format. The Appeal sets out the resource requirements for the regional response and is being disseminated via the PAHO webpage and social media, with direct outreach underway to strategic humanitarian donors. Its objective is to mobilize the financial resources needed to sustain surveillance, immunization, and clinical response activities across affected and at-risk countries. To operationalize the response, the IMST developed a Measles Preparedness and Response Matrix, organizing recommended actions across six technical pillars — Coordination; Surveillance, Laboratory, Case Investigation and Contact Tracing; Clinical Management; Immunization; Risk Communication and Community Engagement; and Rapid Response — differentiated by three epidemiological scenarios (no transmission, characterizable transmission chains, community transmission). The matrix was produced through regional and country office consultation and gives Member States a single reference to calibrate their response posture as local epidemiology evolves.

chunks.text: Despite the overall national declining trend, in recent weeks, transmission appears to be primarily driven by cases reported in a limited number of departments including Guatemala Central, Izabal and Alta Verapaz. The highest incidence rates are observed in Izabal (314.6 cases per 100,000 ↓ declining inhabitants), followed by Guatemala Central (295.5 Sustained per 100,000 inhabitants) and elimination Sololá (289.4 per 100,000 inhabitants). Of all confirmed measles cases, 63% occurred among individuals aged 15–39 years, with the 20–29-year age group being the most affected. Among children under one year of age, those aged 4–11 months accounted for the largest proportion of cases. The sex distribution was relatively balanced, with females accounting for 51% of cases and males for 49%.

chunks.title: Latinoamérica y El Caribe Resumen de Situación Semanal al 31 de julio 2026
sources: UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs
chunks.text: **CIFRAS CLAVE** 3,4M de personas necesitan asistencia alimentaria humanitaria en Venezuela 3,4M de personas podrían enfrentarse a niveles de inseguridad alimentaria de crisis (CIF 3) o emergencia (CIF 4) en Haití 9,7K personas permanecen aisladas en Coquimbo, Chile, debido a fuertes tormentas **VENEZUELA: TERREMOTO** Las necesidades humanitarias siguen elevadas en Venezuela tras los terremotos del 24 de junio, ya que los hogares afectados continúan recuperándose de desplazamientos, pérdidas de medios de vida e interrupciones en el acceso a alimentos. La Red de Sistemas de Alerta Temprana contra la Hambruna (FEWS NET) estima que entre 3,0 y 3,49 millones de personas necesitan asistencia alimentaria humanitaria, y que el terremoto ha provocado resultados de Crisis (Fase 3 de la CIF) en los estados más afectados. Las evaluaciones rápidas indican que muchas familias afectadas han reducido el consumo de alimentos, incluyendo la reducción de las porciones y el salto de comidas para priorizar a los niños. Los socios humanitarios continúan ampliando la asistencia, con el PMA alcanzando a más de 120.000 personas a través de comidas calientes, cestas de alimentos, raciones listas para comer y vales electrónicos.

chunks.title: Latinoamérica y El Caribe Resumen de Situación Semanal al 31 de julio 2026
sources: UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs
chunks.text: Las evaluaciones rápidas indican que muchas familias afectadas han reducido el consumo de alimentos, incluyendo la reducción de las porciones y el salto de comidas para priorizar a los niños. Los socios humanitarios continúan ampliando la asistencia, con el PMA alcanzando a más de 120.000 personas a través de comidas calientes, cestas de alimentos, raciones listas para comer y vales electrónicos. A pesar de la respuesta en curso, persisten importantes necesidades de seguridad alimentaria mientras los hogares reconstruyen sus medios de vida y el acceso a los mercados y servicios básicos sigue siendo limitado. **CHILE: LLUVIAS INTENSAS** Las operaciones de respuesta continúan en Chile tras el clima severo que comenzó a mediados de julio, mientras que un nuevo sistema frontal trae riesgos adicionales de lluvias e inundaciones en varias regiones. Las autoridades han emitido nuevas alertas rojas en partes de Ñuble, Biobío y otras zonas afectadas debido al aumento del nivel de los ríos y a los riesgos de inundaciones y deslizamientos de tierra. En Coquimbo, más de 9.700 personas permanecen aisladas.

chunks.title: Latinoamérica y El Caribe Resumen de Situación Semanal al 31 de julio 2026
sources: UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs
chunks.text: Las autoridades han emitido nuevas alertas rojas en partes de Ñuble, Biobío y otras zonas afectadas debido al aumento del nivel de los ríos y a los riesgos de inundaciones y deslizamientos de tierra. En Coquimbo, más de 9.700 personas permanecen aisladas. El Gobierno también ha declarado una emergencia agrícola en Atacama, Coquimbo y Valparaíso para apoyar los medios de vida afectados, mientras las autoridades continúan los esfuerzos para restaurar infraestructuras, reconectar comunidades aisladas y abordar los impactos de una de las emergencias meteorológicas más severas que han afectado al país en décadas. **REGIONAL: SEGURIDAD ALIMENTARIA** La seguridad alimentaria sigue bajo presión en las zonas vulnerables de Centroamérica y Colombia. En Centroamérica, se prevé que persistan las condiciones de crisis (Fase 3 de la CIF) en el Corredor Seco y en partes de Alta Verapaz y las Altiplano Occidental de Guatemala, donde las pérdidas de cosechas, el agotamiento de las reservas de alimentos y los ingresos por debajo de la media han aumentado la dependencia de estrategias negativas de afrontamiento. La Red de Sistemas de Alerta Temprana contra la Hambruna (FEWS NET) estima que entre 2,0 y 2,49 millones de personas en Guatemala necesitarán asistencia alimentaria entre junio y septiembre.

sources: UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs
chunks.text: En Centroamérica, se prevé que persistan las condiciones de crisis (Fase 3 de la CIF) en el Corredor Seco y en partes de Alta Verapaz y las Altiplano Occidental de Guatemala, donde las pérdidas de cosechas, el agotamiento de las reservas de alimentos y los ingresos por debajo de la media han aumentado la dependencia de estrategias negativas de afrontamiento. La Red de Sistemas de Alerta Temprana contra la Hambruna (FEWS NET) estima que entre 2,0 y 2,49 millones de personas en Guatemala necesitarán asistencia alimentaria entre junio y septiembre. En Colombia, se prevé que persistan las condiciones de Crisis (Fase 3 de la CIF) en La Guajira y Chocó, donde sequías, inundaciones, inseguridad y precios elevados limitan la producción agrícola, los ingresos y el acceso al mercado. Se prevé que las condiciones de El Niño reduzcan aún más las lluvias y las oportunidades laborales agrícolas, aunque las cosechas estacionales y el empleo a partir de octubre deberían suponer alguna mejora. **HAITÍ: SEGURIDAD ALIMENTARIA** Entre junio de 2026 y enero de 2027, se prevé que entre 3,0 y 3,49 millones de personas enfrenten niveles de inseguridad alimentaria de Crisis (Fase 3 de la CIF) o Emergencia (Fase 4 de la CIF) en Haití. La violencia persistente sigue afectando los medios de vida, la producción agrícola, los mercados y las rutas comerciales, generando altos costos de transporte y limitando el acceso a los alimentos.

chunks.text: Se prevé que las condiciones de El Niño reduzcan aún más las lluvias y las oportunidades laborales agrícolas, aunque las cosechas estacionales y el empleo a partir de octubre deberían suponer alguna mejora. **HAITÍ: SEGURIDAD ALIMENTARIA** Entre junio de 2026 y enero de 2027, se prevé que entre 3,0 y 3,49 millones de personas enfrenten niveles de inseguridad alimentaria de Crisis (Fase 3 de la CIF) o Emergencia (Fase 4 de la CIF) en Haití. La violencia persistente sigue afectando los medios de vida, la producción agrícola, los mercados y las rutas comerciales, generando altos costos de transporte y limitando el acceso a los alimentos. Se prevé que los resultados de Emergencia (Fase 4 de la CIF) persistan entre las personas desplazadas internamente y los hogares muy pobres. chunks.title: Latin America & The Caribbean Weekly Situation Update as of 31 July 2026
sources: UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs
chunks.text: **KEY FIGURES** 3.4M people require humanitarian food assistance in Venezuela 3.4M people could face crisis (IPC 3) or emergency (IPC 4) hunger in Haiti 9.7K people remain isolated in Coquimbo, Chile due to severe storms **VENEZUELA: EARTHQUAKE** Humanitarian needs remain elevated in Venezuela following the 24 June earthquakes, as affected households continue to recover from displacement, livelihood losses, and disrupted access to food. The Famine Early Warning Systems Network (FEWS NET) estimates that 3.0 to 3.49 million people require humanitarian food assistance, with the earthquake driving Crisis (IPC Phase 3) outcomes across the most affected states. Rapid assessments indicate that many impacted families have reduced food consumption, including cutting meal portions and skipping meals to prioritize children. Humanitarian partners continue to scale up assistance, with WFP reaching more than 120,000 people through hot meals, food baskets, ready-to-eat rations, and electronic vouchers.

chunks.text: Rapid assessments indicate that many impacted families have reduced food consumption, including cutting meal portions and skipping meals to prioritize children. Humanitarian partners continue to scale up assistance, with WFP reaching more than 120,000 people through hot meals, food baskets, ready-to-eat rations, and electronic vouchers. Despite the ongoing response, significant food security needs persist as households rebuild livelihoods and access to markets and basic services remains constrained. **CHILE: HEAVY RAINFALL** Response operations continue in Chile following the severe weather that began in mid-July, while a new frontal system brings additional rainfall and flood risks across several regions. Authorities have issued new red alerts in parts of Ñuble, Biobío and other affected areas due to rising river levels, flooding and landslide risks. In Coquimbo, more than 9,700 people remain isolated.

sources: UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs
chunks.text: Authorities have issued new red alerts in parts of Ñuble, Biobío and other affected areas due to rising river levels, flooding and landslide risks. In Coquimbo, more than 9,700 people remain isolated. The Government has also declared an agricultural emergency in Atacama, Coquimbo and Valparaíso to support affected livelihoods, as authorities continue efforts to restore infrastructure, reconnect isolated communities and address the impacts of one of the most severe weather emergencies to affect the country in decades. **REGIONAL: FOOD SECURITY** Food security remains under pressure across vulnerable areas of Central America and Colombia. In Central America, Crisis (IPC Phase 3) outcomes are expected to persist in the Dry Corridor and parts of Alta Verapaz and the Western Highlands in Guatemala, where crop losses, depleted food stocks, and below-average incomes have increased reliance on negative coping strategies. The Famine Early Warning Systems Network (FEWS NET) estimates that 2.0 to 2.49 million people in Guatemala will require food assistance between June and September.

In Colombia, Crisis (IPC Phase 3) outcomes are expected to continue in La Guajira and Chocó, where drought, flooding, insecurity, and elevated prices are constraining agricultural production, incomes, and market access. El Niño conditions are expected to further reduce rainfall and agricultural labour opportunities, although seasonal harvests and employment from October onward should provide some improvement. **HAITI: FOOD SECURITY** Between June 2026 and January 2027, 3.0 to 3.49 million people are expected to face Crisis (IPC Phase 3) or Emergency (IPC Phase 4) levels of food insecurity in Haiti, according to FEWS NET. Persistent violence continues to disrupt livelihoods, agricultural production, markets, and trade routes, driving high transportation costs and limiting food access.

chunks.title: Terremotos en Venezuela: Reporte de situación #31 (31 de julio de 2026, Hora: 05:00 pm)
sources: UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs
chunks.text: **Reporte de situación N.º 31** **Terremotos en Venezuela** **31 de julio de 2026** **Hora: 5:00 pm** **Destacados** **Más de 207.700 personas afectadas por los terremotos accedieron a asistencia humanitaria y servicios esenciales** mediante una respuesta multisectorial coordinada entre organizaciones humanitarias, entidades de las Naciones Unidas, comunidades y autoridades nacionales y locales. Hasta el 24 de julio, las autoridades reportaron **5.546 personas** **fallecidas y 16.740 heridas a causa de los terremotos.** El Sistema de las Naciones Unidas y sus organizaciones socias continúan ampliando la respuesta multisectorial a la emergencia. Para atender las necesidades de **1,3 millones de personas afectadas durante los próximos seis meses.** **Situación general** Venezuela enfrenta una emergencia nacional tras dos sismos consecutivos de gran magnitud (7,2 y 7,5) ocurridos el 24 de junio (18:00, hora local) en la región centro-norte. El primer sismo, de magnitud 7,2, tuvo su epicentro en el eje San Felipe–Yumare–Montalbán (Yaracuy/Carabobo).

chunks.title: Terremotos en Venezuela: Reporte de situación #31 (31 de julio de 2026, Hora: 05:00 pm)
sources: UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs
chunks.text: Para atender las necesidades de **1,3 millones de personas afectadas durante los próximos seis meses.** **Situación general** Venezuela enfrenta una emergencia nacional tras dos sismos consecutivos de gran magnitud (7,2 y 7,5) ocurridos el 24 de junio (18:00, hora local) en la región centro-norte. El primer sismo, de magnitud 7,2, tuvo su epicentro en el eje San Felipe–Yumare–Montalbán (Yaracuy/Carabobo). De acuerdo con una actualización reciente del Servicio Geológico de Estados Unidos (USGS), el segundo sismo, de magnitud 7,5, tuvo su epicentro a 17 kilómetros al oeste de Catia La Mar, frente a las costas del estado La Guaira. **Al 24 de julio, las autoridades reportan 1.500 réplicas.** Hasta el 24 de julio, las autoridades reportaron **5.546 personas fallecidas y 16.740 heridas a causa de los terremotos.** Asimismo, informaron que 17.907 personas perdieron sus viviendas y que 856 edificaciones resultaron afectadas, incluidas 190 que colapsaron. Una evaluación preliminar de la Oficina de las Naciones Unidas para la Reducción del Riesgo de Desastres (UNDRR) estima daños directos a viviendas e infraestructura por aproximadamente **US$37.000 millones,** mientras que estimaciones preliminares del PNUD sitúan los daños físicos directos en US$6.700 millones, equivalentes al 6% del PIB. La respuesta gubernamental continúa centrada en la atención de la población afectada y la gestión de los campamentos transitorios.

chunks.title: Terremotos en Venezuela: Reporte de situación #31 (31 de julio de 2026, Hora: 05:00 pm)
sources: UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs
chunks.text: Una evaluación preliminar de la Oficina de las Naciones Unidas para la Reducción del Riesgo de Desastres (UNDRR) estima daños directos a viviendas e infraestructura por aproximadamente **US$37.000 millones,** mientras que estimaciones preliminares del PNUD sitúan los daños físicos directos en US$6.700 millones, equivalentes al 6% del PIB. chunks.text: Respuesta Humanitaria por Sector Seguridad Alimentaria  Un mes después de los terremotos que afectaron Venezuela, el PMA continúa proporcionando asistencia alimentaria a las familias afectadas por el desastre. Hasta la fecha, el PMA ha alcanzado a 161.619 personas. Guiado por evaluaciones continuas en La Guaira, Aragua, Miranda y el Distrito Capital, el PMA adapta su respuesta a las necesidades y capacidades de las poblaciones afectadas.  Durante la última semana, el PMA alcanzó a 32.176 personas mediante la distribución de 8.044 canastas alimentarias familiares, suficientes para cubrir las necesidades alimentarias de los hogares durante un mes. El PMA también distribuyó 2.635 kits de alimentos listos para consumir a familias desplazadas en campamentos transitorios, complementando la provisión de desayunos y garantizando el acceso inmediato a alimentos. Además, amplió su apoyo a 27 comedores comunitarios, alcanzando a un total de 7.032 personas a través de esta modalidad.  Asimismo, durante la última semana, el PMA continuó apoyando los tres campamentos transitorios coordinados por las Naciones Unidas mediante la distribución de 36.040 comidas calientes.

En total, durante el período reportado se distribuyeron 426 toneladas métricas de asistencia alimentaria.  Aunque La Guaira continúa siendo la zona más afectada, el PMA ha ampliado su asistencia a otras áreas, incluido el Distrito Capital y Miranda, mientras sigue fortaleciendo los mecanismos de retroalimentación comunitaria y los sistemas de monitoreo para garantizar una respuesta transparente, responsable y centrada en las personas. Oficina de las Naciones Unidas para la Coordinación de Asuntos Humanitarios (OCHA) OCHA | 3 La organización mantiene la operación de letrinas de emergencia, puntos de lavandería y estaciones de lavado de manos, complementadas mediante el abastecimiento regular de agua por camiones cisterna, la gestión de residuos sólidos y la reposición de insumos de limpieza.  Asimismo, UNICEF alcanzó a personas en comunidades afectadas y campamentos transitorios mediante la distribución de kits e insumos de higiene familiar y personal, beneficiando a más de 9.400 personas.  UNICEF está realizando evaluaciones técnicas de las necesidades de las redes de agua en coordinación con el Ministerio del Poder Popular de Atención de las Aguas (MINAGUAS) en los estados Yaracuy, Falcón y Carabobo, sumándose a las evaluaciones ya realizadas en La Guaira y Miranda.  Las acciones en agua, saneamiento e higiene implementadas por OIM se han centrado en garantizar el acceso seguro al agua y promover prácticas básicas de higiene entre las familias afectadas. Como parte de esta respuesta, la OIM distribuyó 2.986 bidones plegables y 284 bidones semiplegables de 10 litros para el almacenamiento seguro de agua, así como 2.206 kits de higiene destinados a reducir riesgos sanitarios y fortalecer las condiciones de salud pública en los espacios de acogida.  Se concreto, a través de la articulación de la Célula de Información y Coordinación Médica (CICOM) y la evaluación hecha por OPS, la instalación por parte de la Cooperación Suiza de una planta de tratamiento de agua por osmosis inversa en el Hospital Dermatológico Martin Vegas. Esta planta beneficiará a 68 pacientes hospitalizados, 120 personas en consultas y 150 trabajadores de la salud.

Fortalecimiento de la capacidad de respuesta asistencial para 40.000 personas. Oficina de las Naciones Unidas para la Coordinación de Asuntos Humanitarios (OCHA) OCHA | 6  OPS/OMS continúa brindando apoyo para la investigación y seguimiento de 29 eventos de notificación de importancia para la salud pública, logrando así el fortalecimiento técnico y logístico en vigilancia epidemiológica, toma, traslado y procesamiento de muestras por el laboratorio, y control de vectores.  OPS/OMS ha fortalecido la capacidad diagnóstica de la red nacional de laboratorios mediante la provisión de reactivos de biología molecular (RT-PCR) y serología por una inversión superior a US$ 34.000, cubriendo 14 enfermedades prioritarias (arbovirosis, virus respiratorios y patógenos zoonóticos como Hantavirus y Leptospira).  OPS/OMS ha brindado apoyo para el desarrollo y proceso de implementación de aplicativo informático para el registro nominal de atenciones médicas facilitando la automatización de los reportes de Enfermedades de Notificación Obligatoria (ENO).  OPS/OMS ha distribuido productos para el tratamiento y almacenamiento seguro del agua al Ministerio del Poder Popular para la Salud (MPPS) para ser distribuida en campamentos priorizados, con una capacidad entregada suficiente para potabilizar 15.120.000 litros de agua. Esto asegurar la disponibilidad de agua segura para aproximadamente 8.400 familias durante un mes, lo que representa un tercio de personas en albergues, mitigando de forma inmediata el riesgo de brotes de Enfermedades Transmitidas por el Agua (ETA) en estos espacios.  OPS/OMS, junto a el MPPS, brindaron una capacitación sobre las pautas de vacunación en campamentos transitorios en el Distrito Capital, con la participación de 109 vacunadores.

chunks.text: **Situation Report No. 31** **Earthquakes in Venezuela** **31 July 2026** **Time: 5:00 pm** **Highlights** **More than 207,700 people affected by the earthquakes** have received humanitarian assistance and essential services through a coordinated multi-sector response involving humanitarian organizations, United Nations agencies, communities, and national and local authorities. As of 24 July, **authorities reported 5,546 deaths and 16,740 injuries** as a result of the earthquakes. The United Nations system and its partner organizations continue scaling up the multisectoral response to the emergency. To address the needs of **1.3 million people affected by the earthquakes over the next six months.** **Situation overview** Venezuela is facing a national emergency following two consecutive major earthquakes (magnitude 7.2 and 7.5) that struck the country's north-central region on 24 June (18:00 local time).

chunks.title: Earthquakes in Venezuela: Situation Report #31 (31 July 2026, Time: 05:00 pm)
sources: UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs
chunks.text: The United Nations system and its partner organizations continue scaling up the multisectoral response to the emergency. To address the needs of **1.3 million people affected by the earthquakes over the next six months.** **Situation overview** Venezuela is facing a national emergency following two consecutive major earthquakes (magnitude 7.2 and 7.5) that struck the country's north-central region on 24 June (18:00 local time). The first earthquake, measuring 7.2, was centered along the San Felipe–Yumare–Montalbán axis (Yaracuy/Carabobo). According to a recent update from the United States Geological Survey (USGS), the second earthquake, measuring 7.5, had its epicenter 17 kilometers west of Catia La Mar, off the coast of La Guaira State. **As of 24 July, authorities reported 1,500 aftershocks.** As of 24 July, authorities reported **5,546 deaths and 16,740 injuries resulting from the earthquakes.** They also reported that 17,907 people lost their homes, while 856 buildings were affected, including 190 that collapsed. A preliminary assessment by the United Nations Office for Disaster Risk Reduction (UNDRR) estimates direct damage to housing and infrastructure at approximately **US$37 billion,** while preliminary estimates from UNDP place direct physical damages at US$6.7 billion, equivalent to 6 per cent of GDP.

chunks.title: Earthquakes in Venezuela: Situation Report #31 (31 July 2026, Time: 05:00 pm)
sources: UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs
chunks.text: According to a recent update from the United States Geological Survey (USGS), the second earthquake, measuring 7.5, had its epicenter 17 kilometers west of Catia La Mar, off the coast of La Guaira State. **As of 24 July, authorities reported 1,500 aftershocks.** As of 24 July, authorities reported **5,546 deaths and 16,740 injuries resulting from the earthquakes.** They also reported that 17,907 people lost their homes, while 856 buildings were affected, including 190 that collapsed. A preliminary assessment by the United Nations Office for Disaster Risk Reduction (UNDRR) estimates direct damage to housing and infrastructure at approximately **US$37 billion,** while preliminary estimates from UNDP place direct physical damages at US$6.7 billion, equivalent to 6 per cent of GDP. The government response continues to focus on assisting affected populations and managing temporary displacement sites. chunks.title: Venezuela (República Bolivariana de): Respuesta a Terremotos - Reporte de Situación #18 (28 al 30 de julio 2026)
chunks.text: El Reporte de Situación No. 18 presenta una actualización sobre la respuesta de la OIM a los terremotos del 24 de junio en la República Bolivariana de Venezuela y cubre el período comprendido entre el 28 y el 30 de julio de 2026. ## Aspectos destacados Entre el 28 y el 30 de julio, la OIM continuó su respuesta multisectorial en campamentos transitorios y comunidades afectadas mediante intervenciones en alojamiento y coordinación y gestión de campamentos, salud, protección, agua, saneamiento e higiene (WASH) y gestión de información. A la fecha, la OIM y Fundación Vivienda Popular han proporcionado **4.627 sets de cocina, 4.232 lonas plásticas, 3.148 lámparas solares, 2.990 bidones plegables, 2.345 baldes, 2.210 kits de higiene, 947 mosquiteros y 821 kits de refugio** a familias afectadas por los terremotos. Los equipos apoyados por la OIM han brindado **7.374 consultas médicas a 6.565 personas afectadas por los terremotos** mediante servicios de salud, salud mental y apoyo psicológico en campamentos transitorios y comunidades afectadas. ## Actividades de la OIM La OIM continuó la cogestión de cinco campamentos transitorios en La Guaira: Campo de Golf, Mare Abajo II, Polideportivo José María Vargas, Playa Grande y César Nieves, apoyando la prestación de servicios, el registro de población, la orientación comunitaria y la coordinación operativa. En Campo de Golf continuaron los avances en la puesta en funcionamiento de la herradura de servicios, la instalación de iluminación solar, la adecuación de un espacio amigable y mejoras de infraestructura.

chunks.title: Venezuela (Bolivarian Republic of): Earthquake Response Situation Report #18 (28 to 30 July 2026)
chunks.text: The eighteenth Situation Report provides an update on IOM’s response to the 24 June earthquakes in the Bolivarian Republic of Venezuela, covering the period from 28 to 30 July 2026. ## Highlights Between 28 and 30 July, IOM continued its multisectoral response in temporary accommodation sites and affected communities through interventions in shelter and camp coordination and management, health, protection, Water, Sanitation and Hygiene (WASH), and information management. To date, IOM and Fundación Vivienda Popular have provided **4,627 kitchen sets, 4,232 plastic tarpaulins, 3,148 solar lamps, 2,990 collapsible water containers, 2,345 buckets, 2,210 hygiene kits, 947 mosquito nets and 821 shelter kits** to earthquake-affected families. IOM-supported teams have delivered **7,374 medical consultations to 6,565 earthquake-affected people** through health, mental health and psychological support services in temporary accommodation sites and affected communities. ## IOM Activities IOM continued co-managing five temporary accommodation sites in La Guaira: Campo de Golf, Mare Abajo II, José María Vargas Sports Complex, Playa Grande and César Nieves, supporting service delivery, population registration, community information services and operational coordination. At Campo de Golf, progress continued on the centralized service hub, installation of solar lighting, establishment of a child-friendly space and infrastructure improvements.

chunks.title: Venezuela: The IRC and the European Union strengthen health and protection response following earthquakes
chunks.text: Health, protection, and psychosocial support services will be implemented in Miranda, La Guaira, and Caracas. The IRC will launch InfoPalante to provide verified information, personalized guidance, and access to safe services. **Caracas, Venezuela, July 31, 2026 —** One month after the devastating twin earthquakes that struck Venezuela on June 24, over 5,500 people have been killed and 16,740 injured. As soon as the earthquakes hit, the European Union partnered with the International Rescue Committee (IRC) to expand essential health and protection services for over 26,000 people affected by the crisis, through a €1 million grant (July–December) from the EU’s Directorate-General for European Civil Protection and Humanitarian Aid Operations (ECHO). *"The earthquakes have devastated entire communities, leaving many families without access to healthcare, protection, and other essential services needed to rebuild their lives. The European Union's vital support, together with the unwavering commitment of our partners on the ground, allows us to rapidly scale up lifesaving services and reach those at greatest risk. This intervention will enable us to stand with the people of Venezuela in the face of unimaginable loss and help communities move toward a safe, dignified, and hopeful recovery,"* **said Nicole Kast, IRC Country Director for Colombia, Venezuela, and Ecuador.** Before the earthquakes, close to eight million people already required humanitarian assistance.

chunks.title: Venezuela: The IRC and the European Union strengthen health and protection response following earthquakes
chunks.text: The European Union's vital support, together with the unwavering commitment of our partners on the ground, allows us to rapidly scale up lifesaving services and reach those at greatest risk. This intervention will enable us to stand with the people of Venezuela in the face of unimaginable loss and help communities move toward a safe, dignified, and hopeful recovery,"* **said Nicole Kast, IRC Country Director for Colombia, Venezuela, and Ecuador.** Before the earthquakes, close to eight million people already required humanitarian assistance. Just four weeks later, that [number has grown by 1.4 million]( EU Humanitarian Aid funding will bolster IRC’s initial emergency response in the hardest-hit areas of La Guaira, Caracas, and Miranda. The IRC and its partners began launching services immediately after the earthquakes hit, delivering essential supplies, supporting frontline workers and providing first aid and primary health care to between 300 and 400 people every day. In partnership with the Venezuelan Association of Christian-Oriented Health Services (AVESSOC) and the PALUZ Foundation, the IRC will expand access to primary care, and sexual and reproductive health services in affected communities.

chunks.title: Venezuela: The IRC and the European Union strengthen health and protection response following earthquakes
chunks.text: The IRC and its partners began launching services immediately after the earthquakes hit, delivering essential supplies, supporting frontline workers and providing first aid and primary health care to between 300 and 400 people every day. In partnership with the Venezuelan Association of Christian-Oriented Health Services (AVESSOC) and the PALUZ Foundation, the IRC will expand access to primary care, and sexual and reproductive health services in affected communities. In partnership with the Foundation for Children Deserving Protection (FUNDALA), the IRC will provide psychosocial support and case management for at-risk populations, including survivors of gender-based violence, and distribute dignity kits. To increase access to vital information, the IRC will launch InfoPalante in Venezuela. Through this digital channel, affected people will be able to access verified information, identify health and protection services and referral pathways and receive personalized, real-time guidance.

Through this digital channel, affected people will be able to access verified information, identify health and protection services and referral pathways and receive personalized, real-time guidance. InfoPalante is part of [Signpost]( a global initiative co-launched by the IRC and Mercy Corps operating around the world that provides reliable and accessible information to people affected by humanitarian emergencies. InfoPalante has been active in Colombia since 2020 and in Ecuador since 2022. **Media contacts** Sylvan Foley ** ** IRC Global Communications ** **

chunks.title: Venezuela (Bolivarian Republic of): Earthquake Response Situation Report #17 (24 to 27 July 2026)
chunks.text: The seventeenth Situation Report provides an update on IOM’s response to the 24 June earthquakes in the Bolivarian Republic of Venezuela, covering the period from 24 to 27 July. ## **Highlights** Between 24 and 27 July, IOM continued its multisectoral response in transitional sites and affected communities through interventions in shelter and site coordination, health, protection, WASH, and information management. During the reporting period, IOM and its partner Fundación Vivienda Popular distributed **343 tarpaulins, 343 kitchen sets, 343 solar lamps, 618 jerry cans, 275 ropes, 275 blankets, 35 mosquito nets, and 33 buckets**, contributing to improved shelter conditions and access to essential items. To date, IOM continues supporting the management of five transitional sites in La Guaira, where **4,538 people remain hosted**, through the provision of multisectoral services, coordination, and needs monitoring. ## **IOM Activities** IOM continued the co-management of five transitional sites in La Guaira, strengthening coordination mechanisms, registration, community participation, and inter-agency coordination. In Campo de Golf, registration of **102 families** was completed and spatial reorganization advanced for the future installation of **100 tents with IsraAID**.

In Campo de Golf, registration of **102 families** was completed and spatial reorganization advanced for the future installation of **100 tents with IsraAID**. In Mare Abajo II, Playa Grande, and César Nieves, infrastructure improvements, registration updates, and transition planning processes continued. Under WASH, coordination advanced for the installation of a **20,000-litre-per-day water storage and treatment system** in Campo de Golf, alongside sanitation improvements, waste management, and sanitary infrastructure enhancements in other sites. To date, **2,170 collapsible jerry cans, 1,091 hygiene kits, and 93 water storage containers** have been distributed.

IOM and its partner Ven Da Tu Mano continued providing primary health care and **psychological first aid (PFA)** through mobile teams, conducting **more than 500 consultations during the reporting period**, including follow-up and referrals for specialized care. Under information management, IOM completed the **DTM Household Survey** in transitional sites.

Under protection, IOM continued providing guidance, legal assistance, documentation support, referrals, and actions to prevent violence against women, trafficking in persons, and sexual exploitation and abuse (PSEA). chunks.title: Venezuela (República Bolivariana de): Respuesta a Terremotos - Reporte de Situación #17 (24 al 27 de julio 2026)
chunks.text: El decimoséptimo Reporte de Situación presenta una actualización sobre la respuesta de la OIM a los terremotos del 24 de junio en la República Bolivariana de Venezuela, con información correspondiente al período del 24 al 27 de julio. ## **Aspectos destacados** Entre el 24 y el 27 de julio, la OIM continuó su respuesta multisectorial en campamentos transitorios y comunidades afectadas mediante intervenciones en alojamiento y coordinación de sitios, salud, protección, WASH y gestión de información. La OIM y su socio Fundación Vivienda Popular distribuyeron durante el período **343 lonas, 343 sets de cocina, 343 lámparas solares, 618 bidones, 275 cuerdas, 275 mantas, 35 mosquiteros y 33 baldes**, fortaleciendo las condiciones de alojamiento y acceso a bienes esenciales. A la fecha, la OIM continúa apoyando la gestión de cinco campamentos transitorios en La Guaira, donde **4.538 personas permanecen alojadas**, mediante la provisión de servicios multisectoriales, coordinación y seguimiento de necesidades. ## **Actividades de la OIM** La OIM continuó la cogestión de cinco campamentos transitorios en La Guaira, fortaleciendo mecanismos de coordinación, registro, participación comunitaria y articulación interagencial. En Campo de Golf se completó el registro de **102 familias** y avanzó la reorganización del espacio para la instalación futura de **100 carpas con IsraAID**.

chunks.title: Un mois après les tremblements de terre au Venezuela, la Croix-Rouge est toujours sur le terrain. | IFRC
sources: International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies
chunks.text: **Protéger les populations contre les épidémies: la surveillance épidémiologique.** Un mois après la catastrophe, les principales menaces pour la santé publique ne se trouvent plus sous les décombres. Elles découlent désormais des conditions de vie précaires des familles déplacées, qui n'ont pas un accès garanti à l'eau potable et vivent dans des abris surpeuplés où les installations sanitaires sont insuffisantes. Des équipes conjointes de la Croix-Rouge espagnole et de la Croix-Rouge vénézuélienne mènent des évaluations dans ces zones afin **d'anticiper les risques sanitaires et de détecter précocement les maladies respiratoires et gastro-intestinales.** Nombre de ces problèmes de santé sont directement liés au manque d'hygiène et à la pénurie d'eau potable. Cette surveillance continue, menée en étroite coordination avec les autorités locales et les organisations partenaires, est essentielle **pour prévenir une crise sanitaire secondaire.** **Reconnecter les familles** Lorsque les tremblements de terre ont frappé, d'innombrables familles se sont retrouvées dans l'angoisse, sans aucune nouvelle du sort de leurs proches.

chunks.title: Un mois après les tremblements de terre au Venezuela, la Croix-Rouge est toujours sur le terrain. | IFRC
sources: International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies
chunks.text: Des équipes conjointes de la Croix-Rouge espagnole et de la Croix-Rouge vénézuélienne mènent des évaluations dans ces zones afin **d'anticiper les risques sanitaires et de détecter précocement les maladies respiratoires et gastro-intestinales.** Nombre de ces problèmes de santé sont directement liés au manque d'hygiène et à la pénurie d'eau potable. Cette surveillance continue, menée en étroite coordination avec les autorités locales et les organisations partenaires, est essentielle **pour prévenir une crise sanitaire secondaire.** **Reconnecter les familles** Lorsque les tremblements de terre ont frappé, d'innombrables familles se sont retrouvées dans l'angoisse, sans aucune nouvelle du sort de leurs proches. L'effondrement des bâtiments et **la coupure des communications** ont aggravé la tragédie, laissant planer l'incertitude déchirante quant au sort d'enfants, de parents ou de frères et sœurs portés disparus. En réponse, les Sociétés nationales de la Croix-Rouge de onze pays (Argentine, Bolivie, Colombie, Costa Rica, Équateur, Guatemala, Honduras, Mexique, Panama, Paraguay et Uruguay) ont activé leurs services de Rétablissement des liens familiaux (RLF). Aujourd'hui, **la Croix-Rouge vénézuélienne traite des milliers de demandes de recherche émanant de personnes à la recherche de proches,** tant au Venezuela qu'à l'étranger. **Un soutien essentiel, souvent invisible** Dans les tout premiers jours qui ont suivi la catastrophe, la Croix-Rouge colombienne, avec le soutien de la Croix-Rouge allemande, a renforcé les télécommunications opérationnelles en installant des équipements radio et des répéteurs afin d'améliorer la couverture du réseau et la coordination dans les zones prioritaires de recherche et de sauvetage.

chunks.title: Un mois après les tremblements de terre au Venezuela, la Croix-Rouge est toujours sur le terrain. | IFRC
sources: International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies
chunks.text: En réponse, les Sociétés nationales de la Croix-Rouge de onze pays (Argentine, Bolivie, Colombie, Costa Rica, Équateur, Guatemala, Honduras, Mexique, Panama, Paraguay et Uruguay) ont activé leurs services de Rétablissement des liens familiaux (RLF). Aujourd'hui, **la Croix-Rouge vénézuélienne traite des milliers de demandes de recherche émanant de personnes à la recherche de proches,** tant au Venezuela qu'à l'étranger. **Un soutien essentiel, souvent invisible** Dans les tout premiers jours qui ont suivi la catastrophe, la Croix-Rouge colombienne, avec le soutien de la Croix-Rouge allemande, a renforcé les télécommunications opérationnelles en installant des équipements radio et des répéteurs afin d'améliorer la couverture du réseau et la coordination dans les zones prioritaires de recherche et de sauvetage. La nouvelle antenne, récemment installée, couvre une grande partie de Caracas et de La Guaira et est reliée à des répéteurs supplémentaires qui étendent la couverture jusqu'à Maracay. Cette infrastructure permet **une communication fluide entre les équipes d'intervention déployées** à La Guaira, Caracas et dans les régions environnantes. **Car, en situation d'urgence, des communications fiables sauvent des vies.** Au-delà des télécommunications, les équipes de la Croix-Rouge poursuivent les évaluations des dégâts et des besoins, exploitent des unités de traitement de l'eau pour approvisionner les organisations humanitaires et distribuent des kits d'hygiène ainsi que des milliers de litres d'eau potable aux familles touchées.

chunks.title: Cruz Roja Española moviliza más de 88 toneladas de ayuda humanitaria a Venezuela
chunks.text: Un primer envío de 45,5 toneladas ha salido desde el Centro Logístico de Cruz Roja en Las Palmas, en un vuelo facilitado y financiado por el programa Puente Aéreo Humanitario de la Unión Europea (“EU Humanitarian Air Bridge”). Más de 35.000 personas se beneficiarán de la ayuda de este primer envío, compuesto por kits de cocina, mosquiteras, lonas plásticas, y contenedores para almacenamiento de agua segura. Al menos durante dos años, Cruz Roja Española seguirá en Venezuela apoyando en la reconstrucción y recuperación de las familias afectadas y de sus medios de vida. **28 de julio de 2026.** Tras un mes de los terremotos que asolaron Venezuela, Cruz Roja Española continúa apoyando a la población afectada, ahora con la movilización de más de 88 toneladas de ayuda humanitaria, de las que una primera parte (45,5 toneladas) partieron este fin de semana desde Las Palmas de Gran Canarias en un avión fletado y financiado por el programa Puente Aéreo Humanitario de la Unión Europea (“EU Humanitarian Air Bridge”). Gracias al apoyo de la Unión Europea se contribuye a asegurar el acceso a artículos de ayuda humanitaria a las familias afectadas, en este caso, a más de 35.000 personas.

chunks.title: Cruz Roja Española moviliza más de 88 toneladas de ayuda humanitaria a Venezuela
chunks.text: Al menos durante dos años, Cruz Roja Española seguirá en Venezuela apoyando en la reconstrucción y recuperación de las familias afectadas y de sus medios de vida. **28 de julio de 2026.** Tras un mes de los terremotos que asolaron Venezuela, Cruz Roja Española continúa apoyando a la población afectada, ahora con la movilización de más de 88 toneladas de ayuda humanitaria, de las que una primera parte (45,5 toneladas) partieron este fin de semana desde Las Palmas de Gran Canarias en un avión fletado y financiado por el programa Puente Aéreo Humanitario de la Unión Europea (“EU Humanitarian Air Bridge”). Gracias al apoyo de la Unión Europea se contribuye a asegurar el acceso a artículos de ayuda humanitaria a las familias afectadas, en este caso, a más de 35.000 personas. Los artículos movilizados por Cruz Roja Española se componen de 15.600 mosquiteras; 18.650 lámparas solares; 7.800 bidones; 34.187 mantas; 10.700 lonas de plástico; 7.124 kits de cocina; 8.714 filtros de agua; 7.852 kits higiene hombres; 10.616 kits higiene mujeres; 2.332 kits de higiene niñas y niños; 8.000.000 pastillas de cloro; 1 ambulancia; 1 minibús; 2 vehículos 4x4 y ordenadores portátiles. **Un mes de respuestas** La primera respuesta de Cruz Roja Española frente a los terremotos fue el despliegue de una clínica de emergencia, que se encuentra operativa en La Guaira, con una capacidad de asistencia para 30.000 personas, desde la que ya se ha prestado **atención sanitaria a más de 3.000 personas, de las que más de 500 han recibido atención psicosocial.** Durante los primeros cuatro meses esta clínica será gestionada por el personal de Cruz Roja Española, con apoyo de personal técnico especializado de Cruz Roja Venezolana, a quien será transferida para dar continuidad a los servicios de salud. La transferencia de servicio será clave para asegurar una atención médica continuada, apoyo psicosocial y prevención de enfermedades, en apoyo y complementariedad a los servicios de salud que han sido afectados. Desde Cruz Roja Española se sigue apoyando a la Cruz Roja Venezolana en la respuesta conjunta a las necesidades humanitarias más urgentes de las personas y familias afectadas por los terremotos, en coordinación con la Federación Internacional de Sociedades de Cruz Roja y Media Luna Roja. **Cruz Roja seguirá en Venezuela** La **presencia de Cruz Roja Española en Venezuela** no finaliza con la cobertura de esta primera fase de emergencia, sino que continuará al menos durante **dos años más,** articulando respuestas en diferentes áreas clave de intervención: **despliegue de personal especializado**; **envío y distribución de artículos de primera necesidad**; respuesta integral en **salud**; **recuperación de medios de vida** y protección y **fortalecimiento de capacidades operativas** de Cruz Roja Venezolana.

Los pasos más inmediatos serán, en el ámbito de la salud, la transferencia de la clínica de emergencia a la Cruz Roja Venezolana, y el apoyo para el restablecimiento de los servicios del Centro Hospitalario de San José, afectados por los terremotos. En el marco de la fase de recuperación y con el objetivo de dar respuesta a las personas que han perdido sus medios de vida, se están identificando acciones para contribuir al restablecimiento seguro y digno de las condiciones de vida de las familias y comunidades afectadas por el terremoto, facilitando el acceso a servicios básicos, medios de vida y vivienda segura. Las 19 personas delegadas de Cruz Roja Española actualmente desplegadas en el país siguen trabajando en la respuesta humanitaria urgente, así como en la identificación de acciones de recuperación temprana. **Sobre Cruz Roja Española** Cruz Roja Española pertenece al mayor movimiento humanitario del mundo.

Colabora con entidades públicas y privadas para que la ayuda llegue a todas las personas que lo necesitan, en cualquier lugar y en el momento oportuno. Su misión es prevenir y aliviar el sufrimiento humano, proteger la vida y la salud y hacer respetar a las personas. Sus más de 231.000 personas voluntarias dan respuesta en 1.263 municipios, lo que permite atender anualmente a más de 11,6 millones de personas en los ámbitos nacional e internacional.

chunks.title: Cruz Roja Española moviliza más de 88 toneladas de ayuda humanitaria a Venezuela
chunks.text: Su misión es prevenir y aliviar el sufrimiento humano, proteger la vida y la salud y hacer respetar a las personas. Sus más de 231.000 personas voluntarias dan respuesta en 1.263 municipios, lo que permite atender anualmente a más de 11,6 millones de personas en los ámbitos nacional e internacional. Todo ello con el apoyo de cerca de 1,3 millones de personas socias, empresas y alianzas en todos los sectores de la sociedad. Cruz Roja Española ha puesto en marcha un Plan de Respuesta para hacer frente a los efectos de la DANA, con una ejecución continuada a tres años que tiene como objetivo principal contribuir a la recuperación, la construcción de resiliencia y el bienestar físico, emocional y social de las personas y comunidades afectadas. El plan, con el que ya se ha llegado a más de 158.000 personas, se está ejecutando en tres fases**:** la primera, ya realizada, derespuesta inmediata**;** una segunda vinculada a larecuperaciónpara la vuelta a la normalidad, y una tercera de fortalecimiento y resilienciapara asegurar que las comunidades y las personas sean más fuertes y estén preparadas ante posibles eventos futuros de emergencias o catástrofes.

chunks.title: AMDA Emergency Relief #5: Earthquakes in Venezuela - 28 July 2026
sources: Association of Medical Doctors of Asia
chunks.text: As of 28 July, AMDA’s relief team has been working to provide aid to those affected by the earthquakes that devastated Venezuela on 24 June. AMDA has been based in Caraballeda, La Guaira, one of the hardest-hit locations since the start of the quake response efforts. The below is the summary of its activities between 20-26 July: ■20-23 July On 20 July, AMDA's relief team treated approximately 50 patients at the temporary clinic in Caraballeda, La Guaira. Together with local medical volunteers, medical services including blood pressure checks and IV therapy were provided during patient consultations.

chunks.text: The below is the summary of its activities between 20-26 July: ■20-23 July On 20 July, AMDA's relief team treated approximately 50 patients at the temporary clinic in Caraballeda, La Guaira. Together with local medical volunteers, medical services including blood pressure checks and IV therapy were provided during patient consultations. The next day, the patient number increased to around 100, while the team underwent staff shuffling. The new team comprised one doctor, two nurses, and a coordinator, who were from Venezuela and Japan. Nurses on the team were constantly busy with wide range of duties such as taking patients' vital signs, administering IV infusions and inhalation therapy, assisting with electrocardiograms (ECGs), and supporting abdominal ultrasound examinations.

chunks.title: AMDA Emergency Relief #5: Earthquakes in Venezuela - 28 July 2026
sources: Association of Medical Doctors of Asia
chunks.text: The new team comprised one doctor, two nurses, and a coordinator, who were from Venezuela and Japan. Nurses on the team were constantly busy with wide range of duties such as taking patients' vital signs, administering IV infusions and inhalation therapy, assisting with electrocardiograms (ECGs), and supporting abdominal ultrasound examinations. Over the course of two days, the clinic treated patients with a variety of medical needs, including those injured during rescue operations and debris removal, individuals seeking to refill their medication for chronic conditions, and patients suffering from hypertension, joint pain, respiratory illnesses, and other health problems. Caraballeda became somewhat quieter than before as many of international relief teams had already completed their work and left. On 22 July, the clinic continued to receive patients with a wide range of medical needs.

chunks.title: AMDA Emergency Relief #5: Earthquakes in Venezuela - 28 July 2026
sources: Association of Medical Doctors of Asia
chunks.text: Caraballeda became somewhat quieter than before as many of international relief teams had already completed their work and left. On 22 July, the clinic continued to receive patients with a wide range of medical needs. They included those seeking treatment for chronic conditions such as hypertension, individuals injured while clearing earthquake debris, people suffering from dehydration, and children experiencing fever, insect bites, or parasitic infections. The AMDA team saw around 100 patients that day as well. On 23 July, the team was joined by a Japanese doctor who arrived from the United States and examined 55 patients in total.

chunks.text: The AMDA team saw around 100 patients that day as well. On 23 July, the team was joined by a Japanese doctor who arrived from the United States and examined 55 patients in total. In addition to patient consultations, the team provided medicines to those who came to receive medication. Among those who visited the clinic were people who spoke of losing family members in the earthquake. Recognizing that many survivors required not only physical treatment but also psychological support, the team also referred them to a psychotherapist.

Working closely with local healthcare professionals and other partners, the team treated approximately 40 to 90 patients daily.

chunks.title: AMDA Emergency Relief #5: Earthquakes in Venezuela - 28 July 2026
sources: Association of Medical Doctors of Asia
chunks.text: Ambassador Yasushi Sato, Ambassador Extraordinary and Plenipotentiary of Japan to the Bolivarian Republic of Venezuela, visited the temporary clinic to observe AMDA's medical activities. ■24-26 July From 24-26 July, AMDA’s relief team continued providing medical assistance at the temporary clinic in Caraballeda. Working closely with local healthcare professionals and other partners, the team treated approximately 40 to 90 patients daily. While respiratory symptoms and body aches were commonly observed among patients, mild dehydration (likely caused by fatigue and the intense heat) was also seen. During the aid work, Venezuelan physicians and medical students working alongside the team shared that they found great fulfillment in being able to provide much-needed medical care at the temporary clinic. Several also expressed their hope to continue supporting relief efforts in La Guaira even after AMDA concludes its mission.

chunks.text: During the aid work, Venezuelan physicians and medical students working alongside the team shared that they found great fulfillment in being able to provide much-needed medical care at the temporary clinic. Several also expressed their hope to continue supporting relief efforts in La Guaira even after AMDA concludes its mission. As 24 July marked precisely one month from the earthquake, all members of the team observed a moment of silence in memory of those affected by the disaster. Even now, the airport in La Guaira, which had served as the main gateway to the capital, Caracas, remains closed. In surrounding areas, many buildings have either collapsed or are at risk of collapse.

Some people are still searching for family members who remain missing, while others continue to live in makeshift tents after losing their homes. The AMDA team will continue to serve the affected communities for the time being.

chunks.title: Water Mission Increases Emergency Safe Water Access in Venezuela Through New Strategic Partnerships
chunks.text: *Over 18,000 People Served and Nearly 300,000 Liters of Safe Water Produced* ***N. Charleston, S.C. — July 27, 2026** –* [Water Mission]( a Christian engineering nonprofit, is scaling their emergency safe water disaster response operations in Venezuela after earthquakes in late June impacted an estimated 6.8 million people with widespread destruction to infrastructure. A month later, Water Mission has installed and is operating water treatment systems at two production locations serving internally displaced people at clinics, schools, churches, and other community sites. These systems are also providing safe, clean water to a robust and growing [mobile water trucking effort]( with 21 additional water distribution sites in communities throughout Caraballeda, Catia La Mar, Macuto, and Naiguata.

chunks.title: Water Mission Increases Emergency Safe Water Access in Venezuela Through New Strategic Partnerships
chunks.text: A month later, Water Mission has installed and is operating water treatment systems at two production locations serving internally displaced people at clinics, schools, churches, and other community sites. These systems are also providing safe, clean water to a robust and growing [mobile water trucking effort]( with 21 additional water distribution sites in communities throughout Caraballeda, Catia La Mar, Macuto, and Naiguata. New and growing strategic global partnerships are aiding this effort and increasing Water Mission’s ability to simultaneously respond to multiple disasters worldwide. [Water Mission was recently welcomed into Integral Alliance,]( a group of 23 global Christian relief and development organizations with specialized disaster response capabilities. Integral members follow a joint disaster response process when disaster strikes, combining their programming, financial, and communications resources, ensuring a more efficient and rapid response capability that reaches more people in need.

chunks.title: UNICEF Venezuela Humanitarian Situation Report No.6 (Earthquake Response), 21–24 July 2026
chunks.text: **Highlights** One month after two powerful earthquakes struck Venezuela’s north-central coast, children and families continue to face the lasting impacts of displacement, damaged infrastructure and disruption to essential services. UNICEF has provided hygiene supplies to 8,906 people and integrated WASH services to 3,237 people; enabled 21,000 people to access primary health care, including 16,006 people vaccinated; and reached 5,282 children and women with nutrition services. UNICEF also supported more than 4,000 children, adolescents and caregivers with child protection services, including 205 referrals for specialized care, while strengthening education support. Through an integrated humanitarian response, UNICEF aims to reach 470,000 people, including 169,000 children, with life-saving assistance and early recovery support.

Through an integrated humanitarian response, UNICEF aims to reach 470,000 people, including 169,000 children, with life-saving assistance and early recovery support. In addition to its US$137.6 million HAC appeal, UNICEF requires an additional US$65.7 million to sustain critical interventions and support the implementation of the 2026 Humanitarian Response Plan Addendum.

chunks.title: Venezuela: Earthquakes - LTC Situation Report (Telecoms) #04 (Reporting period: 15 - 23 July 2026)
chunks.text: *This Situation Report provides an overview of the twin earthquakes that struck Venezuela on 24 June 2026 (magnitudes 7.2 and 7.5), and their impact on telecommunications. It outlines the activities of the WFP-led Logistics and Telecommunications Cluster (LTC)1 Telecoms Area in supporting emergency communications for the humanitarian response. The Cluster is currently not formally activated for this emergency.* **Summary Points** LTC Telecoms in Venezuela is working with government authorities, mobile network operators, internet service providers (ISPs), the UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA), and other partners to restore critical communications, and prioritize support in the most affected areas. LTC Telecoms is strengthening power continuity across response sites through real-time monitoring of battery systems linked to solar-powered internet connectivity.

chunks.title: Venezuela: Earthquakes - LTC Situation Report (Telecoms) #04 (Reporting period: 15 - 23 July 2026)
chunks.text: The Cluster is currently not formally activated for this emergency.* **Summary Points** LTC Telecoms in Venezuela is working with government authorities, mobile network operators, internet service providers (ISPs), the UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA), and other partners to restore critical communications, and prioritize support in the most affected areas. LTC Telecoms is strengthening power continuity across response sites through real-time monitoring of battery systems linked to solar-powered internet connectivity. This provides timely visibility on energy gaps, allowing teams to monitor and take corrective action to keep critical internet connectivity services operational for over 1,400 humanitarian responders and affected communities. Grupo Telefónica has provided a charging kiosk at each of Polideportivo and César Nieves, supporting 48 power-strip connections, enabling affected people to charge mobile phones and other Information Communication Technology (ICT) devices to maintain access to communication, information and basic services. The kiosks will be returned to Grupo Telefónica once the emergency transitions fully into recovery.
