chunks.title: Venezuela Earthquakes: Situation Report #3 (June 30, 2026)
chunks.text: **Key Updates** Project HOPE continues to expand emergency response activities as the death toll rises. Search and rescue operations are ongoing in La Guaira, with Project HOPE's long-time partner, SAMU, supporting complex extrications and assessments alongside national and international teams. Project HOPE mobile medical unit services are operational in La Guaira, and Project HOPE continues to support 14 partner health centers and supply IPC and WASH materials to health facilities in Caracas. More than 10,000 liters of potable water, 1,000 water purification tablets, and 178 family hygiene kits have been distributed with additional relief supplies planned for affected communities.

chunks.title: Venezuela Earthquakes: Situation Report #3 (June 30, 2026)
chunks.text: Project HOPE mobile medical unit services are operational in La Guaira, and Project HOPE continues to support 14 partner health centers and supply IPC and WASH materials to health facilities in Caracas. More than 10,000 liters of potable water, 1,000 water purification tablets, and 178 family hygiene kits have been distributed with additional relief supplies planned for affected communities. Project HOPE’s Rapid Needs Assessment Report identified critical gaps in the local health system and response capacity. **Situation Overview** The humanitarian situation continues to deteriorate as more than 600 aftershocks have been recorded across northern Venezuela since last Wednesday, including a magnitude 5.1 earthquake on the morning of June 29. Continued seismic activity is complicating search-and-rescue operations, limiting humanitarian access, and hampering recovery efforts. Damage to critical infrastructure — including roads, power, telecommunications, water, and health facilities — continue to disrupt the delivery of essential services, put additional pressure on local health workers, and de-stabilize communities.

chunks.title: Venezuela Earthquakes: Situation Report #3 (June 30, 2026)
chunks.text: Continued seismic activity is complicating search-and-rescue operations, limiting humanitarian access, and hampering recovery efforts. Damage to critical infrastructure — including roads, power, telecommunications, water, and health facilities — continue to disrupt the delivery of essential services, put additional pressure on local health workers, and de-stabilize communities. Casualty figures and damage estimates continue to rise rapidly and vary depending on source. At this time, authorities have reported at least 1,900 deaths, more than 10,500 injuries, approximately 12,000 displaced persons, 15,000 people now considered homeless, and more than 850 buildings damaged, including 189 total collapses. Officials expect the death toll to increase.

chunks.title: Venezuela Earthquakes: Situation Report #3 (June 30, 2026)
chunks.text: At this time, authorities have reported at least 1,900 deaths, more than 10,500 injuries, approximately 12,000 displaced persons, 15,000 people now considered homeless, and more than 850 buildings damaged, including 189 total collapses. Officials expect the death toll to increase. In addition, the United States National Aeronautics and Space Administration estimates that 58,000 buildings have been damaged and multiple trusted sources, including the United Nations, estimate that around 50,000 people remain missing. Up to 6.8 million people have been affected by the earthquakes, including 1.8 million in need of humanitarian assistance, in addition to the 7.9 million already in need of assistance before the earthquakes. The emergency response is transitioning from a predominantly lifesaving search-andrescue operation to a combined rescue, humanitarian relief, and early recovery response.

chunks.title: Venezuela Earthquakes: Situation Report #3 (June 30, 2026)
chunks.text: Up to 6.8 million people have been affected by the earthquakes, including 1.8 million in need of humanitarian assistance, in addition to the 7.9 million already in need of assistance before the earthquakes. The emergency response is transitioning from a predominantly lifesaving search-andrescue operation to a combined rescue, humanitarian relief, and early recovery response. With the significant additional pressure on the local health system, three government field hospitals are currently operational, with additional field hospitals established by the United States and India. Officials have identified urgent needs for orthopedic trauma supplies, while emergency medical priorities increasingly focus on trauma surgery, intensive care, post-operative care, infectious prevention and control, and maintaining essential services for patients with chronic conditions. As rescue operations begin transitioning toward recovery, priorities include expanding temporary shelter, restoring health services, strengthening protection and psychosocial support, and coordinating recovery planning to support affected communities over the coming weeks.

Project HOPE’s Rapid Needs Assessment Report identified critical gaps in the local health system and response capacity. The following sections detail Project HOPE’s cumulative response efforts. Search and Rescue Operations Project HOPE's long-standing partner, SAMU First Response Team, arrived in Caracas on Saturday evening with a team of urban search-and-rescue specialists and K-9 units to support ongoing emergency operations. Project HOPE and SAMU’s search and rescue operations continue alongside Venezuelan authorities and international partners, with complex extrications underway in areas with extensive structural collapse.

chunks.title: Emergency appeal for people affected by the catastrophic earthquakes in Venezuela
chunks.text: Today (Wed 1 July) the Disasters Emergency Committee (DEC) is launching an urgent appeal to raise funds to reach people affected by the catastrophic earthquakes in Venezuela, which have killed at least 1,700 people and left thousands more injured and in need of medical care. The scale of the destruction is catastrophic. Buildings were reduced to rubble in minutes following two back-to-back earthquakes of magnitude 7.2 and 7.5 which struck close to Venezuela’s capital city, Caracas just after 6pm local time on Wednesday 24 June. The second earthquake was the strongest to hit the country in more than a century.

chunks.title: Venezuela earthquakes: Women-led organizations, in partnership with CARE, deliver lifesaving aid
chunks.text: **July 1, 2026, 2026** — CARE is supporting a network of women-led Venezuelan organizations as they respond to two historic earthquakes that devastated the country’s northern coast on the evening of June 24, killing and injuring thousands and leaving widespread destruction and a rapidly growing humanitarian crisis. “After being in La Guaira, the situation is much more dire than we initially thought,” said **Daniella Inojosa of Tinta Violeta**, an organization supported by CARE that specializes in psychosocial support and specialized services for women and children. “The destruction is total. It doesn’t even look like there was ever a city there.” In the aftermath of the earthquakes, Tinta Violeta set up multiple sites in some of the hardest-hit communities to provide targeted support.

chunks.title: Venezuela earthquakes: Women-led organizations, in partnership with CARE, deliver lifesaving aid
chunks.text: “The destruction is total. It doesn’t even look like there was ever a city there.” In the aftermath of the earthquakes, Tinta Violeta set up multiple sites in some of the hardest-hit communities to provide targeted support. At these locations they have been helping survivors cope with the trauma brought on by such a crisis, and distributing essential hygiene supplies and other relief items. They are also providing compassionate care and support for people affected by gender-based violence. Within the first 72 hours of operating in displacement shelters, the organization identified 22 cases of sexual violence, underscoring the heightened risks facing women and girls forced to flee their homes.

Within the first 72 hours of operating in displacement shelters, the organization identified 22 cases of sexual violence, underscoring the heightened risks facing women and girls forced to flee their homes. “The scale of devastation, human loss, and trauma is absolutely heartbreaking, and with search and rescue efforts still continuing, we know the humanitarian needs will continue to grow,” said **Ana Maria Mendez, CARE’s Regional Director in Latin America and the Caribbean**. “Our Venezuelan partners, who we have been working alongside since 2018, began responding in the very first hours after the earthquakes, even as some of their own staff and volunteers were directly affected. They know these communities, understand their needs, and are best placed to lead the response.” The back-to-back earthquakes, measuring 7.2 and 7.5 magnitude, struck near the coastal state of La Guaira, on the outskirts of Venezuela’s capital, Caracas.

chunks.text: “Our Venezuelan partners, who we have been working alongside since 2018, began responding in the very first hours after the earthquakes, even as some of their own staff and volunteers were directly affected. They know these communities, understand their needs, and are best placed to lead the response.” The back-to-back earthquakes, measuring 7.2 and 7.5 magnitude, struck near the coastal state of La Guaira, on the outskirts of Venezuela’s capital, Caracas. The second earthquake was the strongest recorded in the country in more than 125 years. The disaster has compounded an already fragile humanitarian situation in Venezuela, where years of economic and political crisis have forced millions to flee the country. In Venezuela, CARE works entirely through partners and is coordinating directly with them to support communities affected by the disaster, with a particular focus on women and girls, who often face heightened risks during emergencies.

chunks.title: Venezuela earthquakes: Women-led organizations, in partnership with CARE, deliver lifesaving aid
chunks.text: The disaster has compounded an already fragile humanitarian situation in Venezuela, where years of economic and political crisis have forced millions to flee the country. In Venezuela, CARE works entirely through partners and is coordinating directly with them to support communities affected by the disaster, with a particular focus on women and girls, who often face heightened risks during emergencies. These organizations are responding across La Guaira, Caracas, and Carabobo, with relief efforts expected to expand as assessments continue and humanitarian needs evolve. CARE’s partners report that the most urgent needs right now include safe shelter, clean water and sanitation, food, emergency medical care, psychosocial support, protection for unaccompanied children, and safe spaces for women and girls. They also warn that the health system, which was already fragile before the earthquakes, has collapsed in the hardest-hit coastal communities, and is under immense strain in Caracas.

chunks.title: Venezuela earthquakes: Women-led organizations, in partnership with CARE, deliver lifesaving aid
chunks.text: CARE’s partners report that the most urgent needs right now include safe shelter, clean water and sanitation, food, emergency medical care, psychosocial support, protection for unaccompanied children, and safe spaces for women and girls. They also warn that the health system, which was already fragile before the earthquakes, has collapsed in the hardest-hit coastal communities, and is under immense strain in Caracas. Among the other services provided by Tinta Violetais a free hotline for people to call to receive emotional and practical support to cope with this highly traumatic event. Families receive guidance on how to help children navigate post-traumatic stress by encouraging them to express their feelings and slowly set up new routines. “It is normal for children and adolescents to feel afraid, anxious or confused and even change their behaviors after an earthquake,” reads a post on Tinta Violeta’s Instagram account, adding that it’s “fundamental for children to process what has happened, express their emotions, and slowly regain a sense of safety and security.” CARE is also partnering with Grupo Social CESAP — a network of 19 Venezuelan civil society organizations — as well as Humanity & Inclusion, to deliver an inclusive response.

sources: UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs
chunks.text: Al 30 de junio de 2026, los terremotos registrados el 24 de junio en el eje San Felipe–Yumare–Montalbán han generado impactos significativos en personas, infraestructura crítica y vivienda. Las cifras preliminares, aún en proceso de consolidación, reportan más de 22.600 personas afectadas, 13.500 evacuadas, 15.900 personas con viviendas destruidas, 10.600 personas heridas y 1.900 fallecidas. Los daños en infraestructura incluyen 855 edificaciones afectadas, 189 colapsos totales, 38 hospitales con daños y 433 escuelas afectadas, además de aproximadamente 1,2 millones de toneladas de escombros. La situación ha requerido acciones de rescate, evacuación, distribución de agua, instalación de campamentos temporales y despliegue de voluntarios y delegaciones extranjeras.

La situación ha requerido acciones de rescate, evacuación, distribución de agua, instalación de campamentos temporales y despliegue de voluntarios y delegaciones extranjeras. Las prioridades sectoriales identificadas incluyen alojamiento de emergencia, agua, saneamiento e higiene, salud mental y apoyo psicosocial, y referencias de salud y atención médica, debido al incremento de necesidades humanitarias, presión sobre servicios básicos y riesgo de deterioro de las condiciones de vida en las zonas más afectadas. \--- As of 30 June 2026, the earthquakes recorded on 24 June along the San Felipe–Yumare–Montalbán axis have caused significant impacts on people, critical infrastructure and housing. Preliminary figures, still being consolidated, report more than 22,600 people affected, 13,500 evacuated, 15,900 people with homes destroyed, 10,600 injured and 1,900 deceased. Infrastructure damage includes 855 buildings affected, 189 total collapses, 38 hospitals with damage and 433 schools affected, in addition to approximately 1.2 million tonnes of debris.

sources: UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs
chunks.text: Preliminary figures, still being consolidated, report more than 22,600 people affected, 13,500 evacuated, 15,900 people with homes destroyed, 10,600 injured and 1,900 deceased. Infrastructure damage includes 855 buildings affected, 189 total collapses, 38 hospitals with damage and 433 schools affected, in addition to approximately 1.2 million tonnes of debris. The situation has required rescue operations, evacuations, water distribution, the setting up of temporary camps and the deployment of volunteers and foreign delegations. Identified sectoral priorities include emergency shelter, water, sanitation and hygiene, mental health and psychosocial support, and health care and medical referrals, due to increased humanitarian needs, pressure on basic services and the risk of deteriorating living conditions in the most affected areas.

chunks.text: AOB Minutes 1. Situation Update Overview On 24 June, Venezuela was struck by two major earthquakes of magnitude 7.2 and 7.5, occurring 40 seconds apart, with the epicentre located 23 kilometres southeast of Yumare, west of Caracas. Several aftershocks have continued to affect the country. The earthquakes caused significant damage to homes, public buildings, and critical infrastructure, including power and telecommunications networks. Maiquetía International Airport remains closed due to damage, with commercial flights suspended until at least 02 July, while all other airports remain operational.

chunks.pdf_filename: 4218733_2728652_Venezuela Earthquakes Global LTC Telecoms teleconference #1 minutes 29 June 2026.pdf
chunks.text: The earthquakes caused significant damage to homes, public buildings, and critical infrastructure, including power and telecommunications networks. Maiquetía International Airport remains closed due to damage, with commercial flights suspended until at least 02 July, while all other airports remain operational. Following the declaration of a state of emergency, the Government continues to prioritize search and rescue efforts and is coordinating the deployment of international rescue teams and emergency equipment from at least 27 countries. Humanitarian responders are supporting search and rescue operations on the ground. While authorities have permitted the entry of search and rescue teams and selected emergency responders, broader humanitarian access remains limited and uncertain.

chunks.text: Humanitarian responders are supporting search and rescue operations on the ground. While authorities have permitted the entry of search and rescue teams and selected emergency responders, broader humanitarian access remains limited and uncertain. Telecommunications status Telecommunications services remain significantly disrupted nationwide following the 24 June twin earthquakes. Damage to telecommunications infrastructure and interdependent power systems caused a sharp decline in internet connectivity across the country, including in Caracas. Available data indicates national connectivity dropped from approximately 90 percent to between 20 and 30 percent immediately after the earthquakes on 24 June, before partially recovering to an average of around 70 percent by 25 June.

Telecommunications disruptions continue to hamper coordination among search and rescue teams and humanitarian responders. Power and connectivity systems remain highly interdependent and unstable, resulting in intermittent service restoration across affected areas. Connectivity at Maiquetía International Airport has reportedly been partially restored, although the reliability and coverage of services remain under assessment. Venezuela's three national mobile network operators (Movistar, Digitel and Cantv) have implemented measures to support affected populations.

chunks.text: Connectivity at Maiquetía International Airport has reportedly been partially restored, although the reliability and coverage of services remain under assessment. Venezuela's three national mobile network operators (Movistar, Digitel and Cantv) have implemented measures to support affected populations. Cantv has reportedly partnered with SpaceX to provide temporary internet connectivity in La Guaira through Starlink devices, while Movistar and Digitel offered complimentary calls and SMS services for 48 hours following the earthquakes. However, these measures have not fully mitigated ongoing outages, network congestion and service instability. 2. chunks.title: ACNUR refuerza su respuesta en Venezuela ante las crecientes vulnerabilidades provocadas por los terremotos
chunks.text: GINEBRA – La evaluación inicial de necesidades realizada sobre el terreno en Venezuela ha revelado un aumento drástico de las necesidades humanitarias y de protección en los últimos días, mientras los equipos valoran el impacto total de los devastadores terremotos de la semana pasada. En La Guaira, el estado más afectado, escasean los alimentos, los servicios básicos han colapsado y la conectividad se ha visto interrumpida en gran medida. Las tensiones en la comunidad están aumentando, ya que el acceso a la asistencia sigue siendo limitado. ACNUR, la Agencia de la ONU para los Refugiados, se ha movilizado de inmediato para apoyar a las comunidades afectadas y, durante los días 26 y 27 de junio, llevó a cabo una evaluación rápida de necesidades con participantes de La Guaira, el Distrito Capital, Miranda, Aragua y Carabobo.

Las conclusiones iniciales arrojan que: El 75 por ciento de los encuestados informó de heridos en sus comunidades; el 56 por ciento reportó muertes. Las personas de edad avanzada y personas con discapacidad se enfrentan a riesgos agravados debido a la movilidad reducida y el acceso limitado a información digital. ACNUR está intensificando la asistencia de emergencia y los servicios de protección en múltiples frentes. chunks.text: UNHCR scales up response in Venezuela amid growing post-earthquake vulnerabilities

chunks.title: UNHCR scales up response in Venezuela amid growing post-earthquake vulnerabilities
chunks.text: *This is a summary of what was said by UNHCR spokesperson Carlotta Wolf – to whom quoted text may be attributed – at today's press briefing at the Palais des Nations in Geneva.* GENEVA – Initial, on-the-ground needs assessments from Venezuela have revealed a dramatic surge in humanitarian and protection needs in recent days as teams evaluate the full impact of last week’s devastating earthquakes. In La Guaira – the hardest-hit state – food shortages are widespread, basic services have broken down, and connectivity has been largely severed. Community tensions are rising as access to assistance remains constrained. UNHCR, the UN Refugee Agency, has immediately mobilized to support affected communities, and conducted a rapid needs assessment on 26-27 June with participants across La Guaira, the Capital District, Miranda, Aragua, and Carabobo states.

chunks.title: UNHCR scales up response in Venezuela amid growing post-earthquake vulnerabilities
chunks.text: Community tensions are rising as access to assistance remains constrained. UNHCR, the UN Refugee Agency, has immediately mobilized to support affected communities, and conducted a rapid needs assessment on 26-27 June with participants across La Guaira, the Capital District, Miranda, Aragua, and Carabobo states. The initial findings showed that: 75 per cent of respondents had reported injuries in their communities; 56 per cent reported fatalities. Older people and those with disabilities face compounded risks, due to limited mobility and reduced access to digital information. Half of those assessed are staying with neighbours or relatives, 39 per cent are living in streets and public spaces, and others in churches, schools, or improvised facilities.

chunks.title: UNHCR scales up response in Venezuela amid growing post-earthquake vulnerabilities
chunks.text: Older people and those with disabilities face compounded risks, due to limited mobility and reduced access to digital information. Half of those assessed are staying with neighbours or relatives, 39 per cent are living in streets and public spaces, and others in churches, schools, or improvised facilities. Improvised shelters do not meet minimum protection standards, for example for privacy, safe spaces and basic levels of hygiene and comfort. 17 per cent of those surveyed reported the presence of unaccompanied or separated children in their communities. The UNHCR-led Protection Cluster has launched a campaign to address child protection risks, particularly family separation. Efforts focus on awareness-raising, identification, family tracing, and ensuring children’s safety.

chunks.title: UNHCR scales up response in Venezuela amid growing post-earthquake vulnerabilities
chunks.text: The UNHCR-led Protection Cluster has launched a campaign to address child protection risks, particularly family separation. Efforts focus on awareness-raising, identification, family tracing, and ensuring children’s safety. UNHCR is scaling up life-saving assistance and protection services across multiple fronts. We are supporting local authorities with tools and equipment for the safe collection and management of information on affected people, helping identify specific needs and facilitate referrals to appropriate services. At the same time, emergency supplies are being transported from UNHCR’s local warehouse in Táchira to La Guaira, with additional capacity to mobilize more than 20 tonnes of relief items from UNHCR’s global stockpiles in Panama to further bolster assistance.

UNHCR partner CARITAS has established a donation collection and storage centre at the Episcopal Conference premises, including with UNHCR tents and a rub hall, to support aid distributions. Authorities have confirmed 1,719 fatalities, at least 5,034 people injured, and 15,866 people affected as of 29 June. chunks.title: Venezuela (República Bolivariana de): Respuesta a Terremotos - Reporte de Situación #3 (30 de junio de 2026)
chunks.text: Este tercer Informe de Situación presenta una actualización sobre el impacto de los terremotos del 24 de junio en la República Bolivariana de Venezuela y resume las actividades en curso y la respuesta planificada de la OIM en apoyo a las poblaciones afectadas y a los esfuerzos nacionales. **Aspectos destacados** Las cifras oficiales reportan al menos 1.943 personas fallecidas, 10.571 personas heridas, 15.866 personas severamente afectadas y 6.461 personas rescatadas tras los terremotos del 24 de junio. Al menos 855 edificaciones se mantienen reportadas como afectadas, incluyendo 189 colapsos totales, mientras que los daños a viviendas continúan generando necesidades de alojamiento temporal y desplazamiento. La OIM continúa apoyando actividades de alojamiento temporal, agua, saneamiento e higiene, salud, salud mental, protección y gestión de datos, incluida la verificación de 15 de los 39 campamentos transitorios identificados, el apoyo a la coordinación de sitios y el monitoreo de movimientos de población hacia otros estados. **Actividades de la OIM** La OIM ha continuado apoyando acciones de alojamiento, gestión de sitios y servicios esenciales en campamentos transitorios. En coordinación con socios y autoridades, se ha avanzado en el mapeo de 39 campamentos transitorios, de los cuales 15 han sido verificados por la OIM junto con el Grupo de Trabajo de Infraestructura y Alojamientos Temporales.

En coordinación con socios y autoridades, se ha avanzado en el mapeo de 39 campamentos transitorios, de los cuales 15 han sido verificados por la OIM junto con el Grupo de Trabajo de Infraestructura y Alojamientos Temporales. En el Polideportivo José María Vargas, la OIM y las autoridades establecieron espacios de gestión del sitio, recepción, derivación, almacenamiento, triaje médico y protección; además, se entregaron 180 literas y se están activando servicios de protección. También se han identificado necesidades prioritarias en sitios mapeados, incluyendo agua, artículos de higiene, materiales de limpieza, medicamentos, baños, duchas, ropa, artículos para niñas y niños, apoyo eléctrico y capacidad adicional de alojamiento. En Salud, Salud Mental, WASH, protección y datos, la OIM ha mantenido el apoyo a servicios de salud de emergencia y monitoreo de necesidades en sitios prioritarios.

chunks.title: Venezuela (República Bolivariana de): Respuesta a Terremotos - Reporte de Situación #3 (30 de junio de 2026)
chunks.text: También se han identificado necesidades prioritarias en sitios mapeados, incluyendo agua, artículos de higiene, materiales de limpieza, medicamentos, baños, duchas, ropa, artículos para niñas y niños, apoyo eléctrico y capacidad adicional de alojamiento. En Salud, Salud Mental, WASH, protección y datos, la OIM ha mantenido el apoyo a servicios de salud de emergencia y monitoreo de necesidades en sitios prioritarios. En el Polideportivo José María Vargas, en La Guaira, se brindó asistencia médica a 62 personas mediante servicios de pediatría, medicina general y ginecología, incluidas dos derivaciones a establecimientos de salud. A través de la organización socia Ven Da Tu Mano, se apoyó una jornada médica en el campamento transitorio instalado en el Estadio de Béisbol Menor de Maiquetía, donde aproximadamente 150 familias desplazadas se encuentran alojadas. La OIM también desplegó personal de protección, participó en espacios de coordinación del Clúster de Protección, desarrolló herramientas de registro, elaboró mapas de campamentos transitorios y mantuvo el monitoreo remoto de movilidad y de flujos en zonas fronterizas. **Respuesta planificada de la OIM** La respuesta planificada de la OIM continuará priorizando el alojamiento de emergencia y artículos de primera necesidad, la gestión de sitios, salud y SMAPS, WASH, protección, y datos y evaluaciones de necesidades.

chunks.title: Venezuela (Bolivarian Republic of): Earthquake Response Situation Report #3 (30 June 2026)
chunks.text: This third Situation Report provides an updated overview of the impact of the 24 June earthquakes in the Bolivarian Republic of Venezuela and outlines IOM’s ongoing and planned response in support of affected populations and national efforts. **Highlights** Official figures report at least 1,943 fatalities, 10,571 injuries, 15,866 people severely affected and 6,461 people rescued following the 24 June earthquakes. At least 855 buildings remain reported as affected, including 189 total collapses, while damage to housing and urban infrastructure continues to drive displacement and temporary accommodation needs. IOM continues supporting temporary accommodation, WASH, health, mental health, protection and data activities, including the verification of 15 of 39 mapped temporary accommodation sites, site coordination support and monitoring of population movements towards other states. **IOM activities** IOM has continued supporting shelter, site coordination and essential services in temporary accommodation sites. IOM and partners have mapped 39 temporary accommodation sites, of which 15 have been verified together with the Infrastructure and Temporary Accommodation Working Group.

chunks.title: Venezuela (Bolivarian Republic of): Earthquake Response Situation Report #3 (30 June 2026)
chunks.text: IOM continues supporting temporary accommodation, WASH, health, mental health, protection and data activities, including the verification of 15 of 39 mapped temporary accommodation sites, site coordination support and monitoring of population movements towards other states. **IOM activities** IOM has continued supporting shelter, site coordination and essential services in temporary accommodation sites. IOM and partners have mapped 39 temporary accommodation sites, of which 15 have been verified together with the Infrastructure and Temporary Accommodation Working Group. Newly mapped sites in La Guaira include schools and institutional facilities hosting affected families, with reported needs including water, hygiene items, cleaning materials, medicines, toilets, showers, child-focused items, clothing and additional sleeping capacity. At Polideportivo José María Vargas, IOM and authorities have supported the establishment of site management, reception, referral, warehouse, medical triage and protection spaces, with 180 bunk beds delivered and key protection services being activated. In health, MHPSS, WASH, protection and data, IOM has provided health assistance at Polideportivo José María Vargas, reaching 62 people with paediatrics, general medicine and gynaecology services, including two referrals to health facilities.

chunks.title: Venezuela (Bolivarian Republic of): Earthquake Response Situation Report #3 (30 June 2026)
chunks.text: At Polideportivo José María Vargas, IOM and authorities have supported the establishment of site management, reception, referral, warehouse, medical triage and protection spaces, with 180 bunk beds delivered and key protection services being activated. In health, MHPSS, WASH, protection and data, IOM has provided health assistance at Polideportivo José María Vargas, reaching 62 people with paediatrics, general medicine and gynaecology services, including two referrals to health facilities. Through partner organization Ven Da Tu Mano, IOM also supported a medical brigade at the temporary site installed in the Minor Baseball Stadium of Maiquetía, where approximately 150 displaced families are sheltering. IOM has also deployed protection staff, supported coordination with site management teams, participated in Protection Cluster discussions, maintained DTM-based mapping and mobility monitoring, and reported movements of internally displaced families from La Guaira towards municipalities in Zulia, including Maracaibo, San Francisco, Rosario de Perijá and Cabimas. **IOM planned response** IOM’s planned response will continue to prioritize emergency accommodation and core relief items, site coordination and management, health and MHPSS, WASH, protection, and data and needs assessments. In site coordination, IOM will continue monitoring, service mapping and verification of temporary accommodation sites, support site planning, population registration and digitalization of registration, and strengthen community organization, coexistence rules, information provision, AAP, GBV and PSEA measures.

chunks.title: Venezuela (Bolivarian Republic of): Earthquake Response Situation Report #3 (30 June 2026)
chunks.text: IOM has also deployed protection staff, supported coordination with site management teams, participated in Protection Cluster discussions, maintained DTM-based mapping and mobility monitoring, and reported movements of internally displaced families from La Guaira towards municipalities in Zulia, including Maracaibo, San Francisco, Rosario de Perijá and Cabimas. **IOM planned response** IOM’s planned response will continue to prioritize emergency accommodation and core relief items, site coordination and management, health and MHPSS, WASH, protection, and data and needs assessments. In site coordination, IOM will continue monitoring, service mapping and verification of temporary accommodation sites, support site planning, population registration and digitalization of registration, and strengthen community organization, coexistence rules, information provision, AAP, GBV and PSEA measures. IOM will also support site improvements and the delivery of tents, tarpaulins and basic arrangements to improve safety, dignity and protection. Across health, WASH, protection and data, IOM will continue mobile health activities in temporary accommodation sites, including general medicine, paediatrics, gynaecology and obstetrics, psychological first aid and referrals. IOM will prioritize medicines, supplies, referral pathways for severe medical cases and persons with reduced mobility, while maintaining MHPSS support, WASH interventions, hygiene kits, water storage, handwashing spaces, sanitation, waste management and infection prevention and control.

chunks.title: Un cargamento de ayuda de UNICEF llega a Venezuela tras los catastróficos terremotos
chunks.text: ## Un cargamento de 47 toneladas métricas de suministros de salud, agua y educación fue movilizado desde el depósito de la EU en Copenhague; se espera que llegue más ayuda en los próximos días. **CARACAS/COPENHAGUE/NUEVA YORK, 30 de junio de 2026 –** En respuesta a los catastróficos terremotos que afectaron a Venezuela el 24 de junio, un cargamento de 47 toneladas métricas de suministros humanitarios de UNICEF ha llegado hoy al país para apoyar a los niños, niñas y las familias afectadas. El cargamento —movilizado desde el depósito de la Unión Europea alojado en el centro mundial de suministros y logística de UNICEF en Copenhague— incluye kits de salud de emergencia para atención médica urgente, incluyendo suministros para partos seguros, cuidado del recién nacido, prevención y tratamiento de enfermedades; suministros de purificación y almacenamiento de agua para contribuir a proporcionar agua potable segura; carpas para establecer espacios amigables para la infancia y puntos de servicios; ayudas para la movilidad, incluyendo sillas de ruedas; y materiales de recreación y desarrollo infantil temprano para ayudar a los niños y niñas a recuperar la sensación de normalidad y continuar aprendiendo. "Este cargamento no podría llegar en un momento más crítico para los niños de Venezuela," afirmó Roberto Benes, Director Regional de UNICEF para América Latina y el Caribe. "Las familias de los estados afectados necesitan urgentemente agua segura, así como acceso a atención de salud.

chunks.title: Un cargamento de ayuda de UNICEF llega a Venezuela tras los catastróficos terremotos
chunks.text: "Este cargamento no podría llegar en un momento más crítico para los niños de Venezuela," afirmó Roberto Benes, Director Regional de UNICEF para América Latina y el Caribe. "Las familias de los estados afectados necesitan urgentemente agua segura, así como acceso a atención de salud. Muchas están durmiendo al aire libre, con miedo a nuevas réplicas. Estos suministros nos ayudarán a llegar a los niños y familias con lo que más necesitan en este momento —atención médica, agua limpia, espacios seguros. Pero las necesidades sobre el terreno son mucho mayores que lo que ha llegado hoy, y necesitamos apoyo sostenido para seguir ampliando nuestra respuesta." Se estima que aproximadamente 680,000 niños necesitan asistencia humanitaria en los seis estados afectados por los terremotos —que fueron el evento sísmico más significativo que ha afectado a Venezuela en más de un siglo.

Las comunidades continúan en riesgo por las réplicas persistentes, que han superado las 600 desde los terremotos iniciales. Este cargamento, junto con uno regional que llegó desde Panamá el 28 de junio, apoyará a más de 100,000 niños y familias durante un período de tres meses. UNICEF continúa coordinando con las autoridades nacionales, el Equipo de País de las Naciones Unidas y socios humanitarios para evaluar necesidades y ampliar la respuesta en protección de la infancia, salud, nutrición y WASH.

UNICEF estima que se requieren 52 millones de dólares estadounidenses para responder a la emergencia por el terremoto, como parte de su más amplio llamamiento de Acción Humanitaria para la Infancia 2026 para Venezuela, que asciende a 137,6 millones de dólares estadounidenses y que, antes de los terremotos, contaba solo con un 35 por ciento de financiación. UNICEF ha movilizado aproximadamente 3,5 millones de dólares estadounidenses de sus propios fondos de emergencia interna para permitir el despliegue inicial rápido de suministros y personal. \## ## Contactos de prensa **Sendai Carolina Zea** UNICEF Latin America and the Caribbean Teléfono: +507 6821 0843 Correo electrónico: **Giacomo Colarullo** Oficial de comunicación UNICEF Teléfono: +1 917 622 2782 Correo electrónico:

chunks.title: WFP amplía la asistencia a las familias afectadas por los terremotos de Venezuela
chunks.text: **CARACAS, Venezuela –** El Programa Mundial de las Naciones Unidas (WFP) está ampliando rápidamente sus operaciones en Venezuela y aumentando la asistencia alimentaria con el objetivo de llegar a hasta medio millón de personas en las zonas más afectadas por los terremotos de la semana pasada. Miles de personas se han visto desplazadas tras los dos potentes terremotos que sacudieron el país el 24 de junio, destruyendo viviendas, infraestructuras y medios de subsistencia en al menos siete estados. Muchas familias se encuentran ahora refugiadas en centros de evacuación abarrotados, donde las necesidades de alimentos, agua potable, refugio y servicios básicos aumentan día a día. WFP ha puesto en marcha distribuciones de alimentos en La Guaira, el estado más afectado, proporcionando hasta ahora paquetes que contienen raciones alimentarias para un mes (cereales, legumbres y aceite vegetal) a 1 200 personas, y ha establecido centros de alimentación temporales en el estado.

chunks.title: WFP amplía la asistencia a las familias afectadas por los terremotos de Venezuela
chunks.text: Muchas familias se encuentran ahora refugiadas en centros de evacuación abarrotados, donde las necesidades de alimentos, agua potable, refugio y servicios básicos aumentan día a día. WFP ha puesto en marcha distribuciones de alimentos en La Guaira, el estado más afectado, proporcionando hasta ahora paquetes que contienen raciones alimentarias para un mes (cereales, legumbres y aceite vegetal) a 1 200 personas, y ha establecido centros de alimentación temporales en el estado. Estos centros agrupan los servicios humanitarios en un único lugar, lo que permite a las comunidades afectadas acceder a la asistencia alimentaria y recibir apoyo de la OIM y UNICEF para otras necesidades esenciales. «En La Guaira, las viviendas, los mercados y las reservas de alimentos han quedado devastados, lo que ha dejado a las familias con poco o nada que comer», afirmó Stephanie Hochstetter, directora nacional de WFP en Venezuela. «En estos momentos, además de los servicios médicos de emergencia, el acceso a alimentos, agua y refugio son las prioridades más urgentes. Los equipos de WFP trabajan sin descanso para hacer llegar a los supervivientes la ayuda que necesitan desesperadamente». A medida que se va conociendo mejor la magnitud de la emergencia, WFP también está ampliando sus operaciones más allá de La Guaira a otras zonas afectadas del país.

A medida que se va conociendo mejor la magnitud de la emergencia, WFP también está ampliando sus operaciones más allá de La Guaira a otras zonas afectadas del país. Se están desplegando equipos de WFP para evaluar las condiciones sobre el terreno y planificar una posible asistencia alimentaria adicional allí donde se considere necesario. WFP también está apoyando la respuesta humanitaria en general a través de su capacidad logística, ayudando a transportar suministros, proporcionando capacidad de almacenamiento y mejorando la conectividad en zonas donde las carreteras, los servicios y las infraestructuras han resultado dañadas. WFP lleva cinco años prestando apoyo humanitario esencial en Venezuela, y en 2025 ha atendido a más de 760 000 personas en 12 estados.

chunks.title: Earthquake leaves Venezuela in ruins as approximately 50,000 remain missing and survivors go without water
chunks.text: ## In Caracas and La Guaira families are sleeping in the streets and parks, searching rubble with bare hands, and competing for clean water as the survival window closes Almost 50,0000 people, including children remain missing under rubble, with rescue workers racing against a closing survival window, IRC teams most concerned about elevated risks to children. Authorities report 12,721 people have been displaced and 774 buildings have collapsed. The national water system has failed across seven states, putting survivors, the injured, and rescue workers at risk. Families fled with nothing; Women and children in shelters have no documents, no medication, nowhere to return.

chunks.title: Earthquake leaves Venezuela in ruins as approximately 50,000 remain missing and survivors go without water
chunks.text: The national water system has failed across seven states, putting survivors, the injured, and rescue workers at risk. Families fled with nothing; Women and children in shelters have no documents, no medication, nowhere to return. Some collapsed buildings may contain survivors but the critical window has closed; international crews continue extracting survivors from the rubble as late as Monday. **Caracas, Venezuela, June 30, 2026** — Almost a week after two powerful earthquakes struck Venezuela, and roughly 48 hours after the critical 72-hour survival window closed, search and rescue operations continue. IRC teams and partners on the ground in Caracas and La Guaira report tens of thousands of people still missing beneath collapsed buildings, and survivors across multiple states struggle to find safe drinking water. IRC is concerned about elevated child protection risks given the scale of missing persons, and is prioritizing family tracing and reunification support.

chunks.title: Earthquake leaves Venezuela in ruins as approximately 50,000 remain missing and survivors go without water
chunks.text: IRC teams and partners on the ground in Caracas and La Guaira report tens of thousands of people still missing beneath collapsed buildings, and survivors across multiple states struggle to find safe drinking water. IRC is concerned about elevated child protection risks given the scale of missing persons, and is prioritizing family tracing and reunification support. The scale of the response does not meet the scale of humanitarian need. Medical services at health centers and mobile units are overwhelmed, shelters are at full capacity, and water and electricity services remain disrupted across the affected areas. A massive but uncoordinated influx of aid has led to significant food spoilage, with distribution points turning away donations due to oversupply.

chunks.title: Earthquake leaves Venezuela in ruins as approximately 50,000 remain missing and survivors go without water
chunks.text: Medical services at health centers and mobile units are overwhelmed, shelters are at full capacity, and water and electricity services remain disrupted across the affected areas. A massive but uncoordinated influx of aid has led to significant food spoilage, with distribution points turning away donations due to oversupply. As search and rescue teams begin to withdraw in the coming days, aid organizations are warning that food needs are expected to resurface and intensify even as the rescue phase winds down. The IRC is scaling its response as field teams report the full scale of destruction becoming clearer with each passing hour. *"What we are seeing in the shelters is heartbreaking; women alone with young children, no documents, no medicine, no idea where their partners or relatives are,"* **said Nicole Kast, IRC Venezuela Country Director.** *"Children are not sleeping. Every aftershock sends collective panic through the shelters, and the psychological toll of that will last long after the rubble is cleared."* The states of Caracas, La Guaira and Miranda have been declared a disaster zone, where teams are witnessing families lined up under the sun for water and food.

IRC partners are also observing a massive flow of people moving toward Caracas, both to assist relief efforts and to search for missing family members. Families are sheltering outdoors rather than risk returning to structurally compromised buildings - a fear made more acute by hundreds of aftershocks since the quake struck, which seismologists warn could continue for three to six months. IRC teams in the Altamira and San Bernardino neighborhoods report witnessing families searching for loved ones in the rubble with their bare hands. chunks.title: Emergency Assistance in Response to the Earthquake Damage in Venezuela
chunks.text: On June 30, upon the request of the Government of Venezuela, the Government of Japan has decided to provide emergency relief goods (plastic sheet (Tarpaulin), portable jerry can, and water purifier) through the Japan International Cooperation Agency (JICA) to Venezuela in response to the earthquake damages. 1. In addition, a JICA survey team has been dispatched to the site since June 26 to assess local medical, recovery, and reconstruction needs. 2. The Government of Japan will continue to stand by the people of Venezuela and stands ready to study further necessary assistance, bearing in mid the human security needs. ## (Reference) In Venezuela, a magnitude 7+ earthquake that occurred on Thursday, June 25, caused numerous casualties, including deaths and injuries, and property damage. According to the Venezuelan government's announcement, the damage includes 1,719 deaths, over 5,034 injuries, and over 885 damaged houses, and the full extent of the damage is still unknown (as of June 30).

chunks.text: Autoridades y expertos nacionales e internacionales realizaron una primera inspección.  Autoridades venezolanas y personal estadounidense realizaron inspección en el puerto de La Guaira.  Estimaciones preliminares indican daños físicos directos por 6.700 millones de dólares, equivalentes al 6 % del PIB, según datos de PNUD.  La conectividad de internet y telecomunicaciones permanece inestable en algunas zonas, afectando la comunicación. Respuesta nacional e internacional  El gobierno venezolano mantiene activos planes de contingencia para salvaguardar la vida de las personas afectadas.  Despliegue masivo de Protección Civil y cuerpos de seguridad, y el sistema de salud público y privado activado a nivel nacional.  Activación de comisión presidencial para la evaluación de habitabilidad de viviendas e infraestructuras, conformado por los ministerios pertinentes, grupos gremiales y sector académico, así como un Estado Mayor para el establecimiento de campamentos transitorios para las personas afectadas. Apoyo internacional:  La respuesta de los equipos USAR continúa. Al menos 49 equipos de búsqueda y rescate de 28 países, con 2.358 efectivos y 189 perros, están desplegados en las zonas más afectadas para apoyar labores de rescate y atención médica.  OCHA presta apoyo logístico a los equipos de búsqueda y rescate en el terreno.  El apoyo internacional continúa: China envía ayuda por un valor de 100 millones de yuanes; Brasil envía cuatro vuelos con ayuda humanitaria; Cuba envía un segundo contingente de rescatistas; Colombia envía otro vuelo con 3.200 elementos de asistencia humanitaria, además de bienestarina y medicamentos; Litutrtriania envía equipo médico y de rescate; Alemania envía un equipo médico en coordinación con las autoridades y la OPS.  Además del apoyo financiero, la Unión Europea activó el Servicio de Cartografía de Emergencia de Copernicus para generar imágenes de alta resolución de las zonas afectadas y producir mapas operativos para los equipos de búsqueda; asimismo, organizó un puente aéreo humanitario para el transporte de aproximadamente 50 toneladas de suministros, incluidos artículos de alojamiento, agua, saneamiento e higiene (ASH) y materiales educativos.  El Banco de Desarrollo de América Latina y El Caribe (CAF) anunció la creación del Fondo para la Recuperación y Reconstrucción de Venezuela con un capital inicial de 1 millón de dólares.  La Federación Internacional de Sociedades de la Cruz Roja y de la Media Luna Roja (IFRC) lanzó un Llamamiento de Emergencia por 50 millones de francos suizos. Medidas adoptadas por las autoridades  Se desplegaron jueces, en coordinación con otras entidades pertinentes, en centros médicos, parques y otros sitios habilitados en la Gran Caracas para la atención de niñas, niños y adolescentes afectados.  Disponible línea de apoyo psicológico para las personas afectadas: 0800-AYUDA-01.  Creación de un formulario digital del Consejo Nacional para las Personas con Discapacidad (Conapdis) para coordinar una respuesta oportuna e inclusiva en las zonas afectadas.  Creación de página web para localizar personas desaparecidas.

Hasta el domingo 28 de junio, el servicio de agua se encontraba a un 68% y la vialidad en un 90%.  Los servicios de salud enfrentan una fuerte presión debido al elevado número de personas heridas.  La morgue del Seguro Social presenta limitaciones de capacidad frente al volumen actual y proyectado.  Agencias de la ONU se encuentran brindando servicios esenciales de forma articulada a la población afectada.  Cinco (5) organizaciones socias del Fondo Humanitario de Venezuela (FHV) con presencia en el estado apoyan la respuesta inicial con servicios de atención primaria en salud y atención psicológica.  El Aeropuerto Internacional de Maiquetía sufrió daños y se mantienen suspendidas operaciones comerciales. Miranda  Se reportan daños en infraestructura, con hasta 33 viviendas y 7 edificios colapsados, en su mayoría en los municipios Chacao, Eulalia Buroz y Plaza.  Las mayores concentraciones de personas damnificadas se registran en los municipios Chacao, Independencia, Brión, Zamora y Eulalia Buroz.  Se reportan afectaciones en infraestructura crítica, incluyendo centros de salud, centros educativos y entes públicos; así como daños en establecimientos comerciales, centros religiosos y deportivos en distintos municipios del estado.  Cuatro (4) organizaciones del FHV con proyectos financiados en municipios del estado y en Distrito Capital apoyan la respuesta inicial con servicios en protección general, de la niñez y de violencia basada en género (VBG). Oficina de las Naciones Unidas para la Coordinación de Asuntos Humanitarios (OCHA) OCHA | 4 Carabobo y Yaracuy (zona del epicentro)  Se reportan daños materiales en ambos estados, con afectaciones en viviendas, edificaciones e infraestructura vial; incluyendo carreteras agrietadas (por ejemplo, la redoma de Morón).  En Carabobo, las principales afectaciones se concentran en el municipio Juan José Mora, especialmente en la parroquia Morón, donde se ubican 9 de los sectores afectados.  A nivel general, se reportan 1.091 personas afectadas y 10 personas fallecidas.  Se contabilizan 170 viviendas afectadas (42 con daños estructurales, 12 con colapso parcial y 11 con colapso total).  Se reportan 12 edificios afectados, de los cuales 9 fueron declarados no habitables y 3 totalmente afectados, incluido el Hotel Tucacas (Falcón).  Cinco organizaciones (Cruz Roja Venezolana, CESAP, Tierra Viva, Cáritas Morón y Empodérame) brindan respuesta en salud, alimentación, agua y distribución de ayuda humanitaria durante esta fase inicial.  Las necesidades preliminares incluyen búsqueda y rescate, evaluación estructural, alojamiento temporal, atención en salud, agua, alimentación, higiene y apoyo psicosocial.

Falcón (Tucacas – Municipio Silva)  Emergencia focalizada en el municipio Silva, atendida por el gobierno regional, que anunció el cese formal de las operaciones de búsqueda y rescate en la parroquia Tucacas (balance oficial de 12 personas fallecidas).  El gobierno regional adelanta un plan integral de atención para 87 familias afectadas (252 personas) en la parroquia Boca de Aroa.  Se reporta la llegada de personas desplazadas desde La Guaira hacia los municipios Miranda y Falcón.  La Cruz Roja Venezolana acompañó las operaciones de búsqueda y rescate, la logística y la atención psicosocial, y Cáritas habilitó un centro de acopio en Coro y apoyó el traslado de insumos.  OCHA mantiene coordinación con las autoridades regionales para identificar oportunidades de colaboración y facilitar oportunamente el apoyo complementario de la comunidad humanitaria.  El Foro Local de Coordinación (FLC), con el apoyo del Foro del estado Zulia, completó un mapeo de capacidades y recursos disponibles y se mantiene preparado para un eventual despliegue. Otros estados  En el estado Apure, se reporta el retorno de población local que se encontraba en los estados afectados; la Gobernación dispuso traslado terrestre a través de diversas instituciones. El Foro Local de Coordinación (FLC) apoya de forma complementaria.  En el estado Delta Amacuro, se articuló con las autoridades la atención psicológica por parte de las organizaciones humanitarias de un grupo de personas afectadas provenientes de Caracas.  En el estado Táchira, las organizaciones humanitarias y las autoridades se reunieron para coordinar acciones e informar sobre la flexibilización de protocolos para la asistencia a la emergencia en Caracas y La Guaira.  En los estados Trujillo y Lara, los espacios para la coordinación humanitaria se preparan en caso de ser requerido.  En el estado Sucre, autoridades desplegaron más de 200 funcionarios de búsqueda y rescate, atención prehospitalaria y logística en apoyo a las zonas más afectadas.

chunks.title: WFP scales up assistance for families hit by Venezuela earthquakes
chunks.text: **CARACAS, Venezuela –** The United Nations World Food Programme (WFP) is rapidly scaling its operations in Venezuela and expanding food assistance aimed at reaching up to half a million people in the areas hardest hit by last week’s earthquakes. Thousands of people have been displaced after two powerful earthquakes struck on 24 June, destroying homes, infrastructure, and livelihoods across at least seven states. Many families are now sheltering in crowded evacuation centers with needs growing for food, clean water, shelter and basic services by the day. WFP has launched food distributions in La Guaira, the worst-affected state, providing parcels that contain one-month’s worth of food rations (cereals, pulses and vegetable oil) for 1,200 people so far and setting up temporary feeding centers in the state.

chunks.title: WFP scales up assistance for families hit by Venezuela earthquakes
chunks.text: “In La Guaira, homes, markets, and food supplies have been devastated, leaving families with little or nothing to eat,” said Stephanie Hochstetter, WFP Country Director in Venezuela. “Right now, in addition to emergency medical services, access to food, water and shelter are the most urgent priorities. WFP teams are working around the clock to reach survivors with the assistance they desperately need.” As the scale of the emergency becomes clearer, WFP is also expanding operations beyond La Guaira into other impacted areas of the country. WFP teams are deploying to assess conditions on the ground and plan for possible further food assistance where it is considered necessary. WFP is also supporting the wider humanitarian response through its logistics capacity, helping to transport supplies, provide storage capacity and improve connectivity in areas where roads, services and infrastructure have been damaged.

WFP is also supporting the wider humanitarian response through its logistics capacity, helping to transport supplies, provide storage capacity and improve connectivity in areas where roads, services and infrastructure have been damaged. WFP has been providing essential humanitarian support in Venezuela for five years, reaching more than 760,000 people in 12 states in 2025. WFP already has more than 3,000 metric tons of food in the country — enough to support more than 10,000 families for two months — and is bringing in additional supplies. In addition, more than 1,400 metric tons of relief items from humanitarian partners are pre-positioned at the WFP-managed United Nations Humanitarian Response Depot in Panama and ready for dispatch.

WFP is urgently appealing for an initial USD50 million to provide emergency food assistance to up to 500,000 people over the next three months. The response will also support logistics and emergency communications. WFP has the capacity to scale up to meet the food needs of one million people, if sufficient funding is secured.

chunks.title: UNICEF aid shipment lands in Venezuela following devastating earthquakes
chunks.text: **CARACAS/COPENHAGEN/NEW YORK, 30 June 2026 –** In response to the devastating earthquakes that struck Venezuela on 24 June, a 47-metric-ton shipment of UNICEF humanitarian supplies has arrived in the country today to support children and families affected. The shipment - mobilized from the European Union stockpile hosted at the UNICEF global supply and logistics hub in Copenhagen - includes emergency health kits for urgent medical care, including supplies for safe births, newborn care and disease prevention and treatment; water purification and storage supplies to help provide safe drinking water; tents for setting up child-friendly spaces and service points; mobility aids including wheelchairs ; and recreational and early childhood development supplies to help children regain a sense of normalcy and continue learning. "This shipment could not come at a more critical time for children here in Venezuela,’ said UNICEF Regional Director for Latin America and that Caribbean, Roberto Benes. "Families across the affected states are in urgent need of safe water, as well as access to health care.

chunks.title: UNICEF aid shipment lands in Venezuela following devastating earthquakes
chunks.text: "This shipment could not come at a more critical time for children here in Venezuela,’ said UNICEF Regional Director for Latin America and that Caribbean, Roberto Benes. Charleston, S.C. — June 29, 2026** –* [Water Mission]( a Christian engineering nonprofit, has a Disaster Assistance Response Team in Venezuela working with partners and authorities to begin an assessment to set up multiple emergency safe water treatment systems. A pair of back-to-back earthquakes caused widespread destruction to infrastructure, collapsing buildings and homes, leaving more than 50,000 people missing and at least 1,450 people who lost their lives. Initial reports indicate that these numbers could rise in the days ahead, with many people believed to be buried in collapsed buildings.

chunks.title: UNDP Estimates 1.2 Million Tonnes of Debris in La Guaira area, After Earthquakes in Venezuela
chunks.text: La Guaira is the worst-affected area after the 24 June earthquakes; figures are expected to be updated as additional data and field assessments become available. **Caracas / New York, 29 June** - As affected communities cope with the loss and devastation caused by the earthquakes, clearing debris is a critical first step toward recovery. An estimated **1.2 million tonnes** of debris resulted from the June 24 earthquakes across the hardest-hit areas of La Guaira state, according to a preliminary assessment by the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP). This analysis is intended to help authorities **with** debris removal and recovery efforts. For families and communities in affected aras, clearing debris is the first step toward restoring access, reopening essential services, and beginning the process of recovery.

chunks.title: UNDP Estimates 1.2 Million Tonnes of Debris in La Guaira area, After Earthquakes in Venezuela
chunks.text: This analysis is intended to help authorities **with** debris removal and recovery efforts. For families and communities in affected aras, clearing debris is the first step toward restoring access, reopening essential services, and beginning the process of recovery. Produced using [**RAPIDA**]( UNDP's rapid assessment tool, the analysis combines satellite imagery, AI-based building damage assessments, building footprint and height data, and local engineering expertise to estimate debris volumes. chunks.title: El PNUD estima 1,2 millones de toneladas de escombros en La Guaira tras los terremotos en Venezuela
chunks.text: **La Guaira es la zona más afectada por los terremotos del 24 de junio. Las cifras se actualizarán a medida que se disponga de nuevos datos y evaluaciones sobre el terreno.** **Caracas / Nueva York, 29 de junio** – Mientras las comunidades afectadas enfrentan las pérdidas y la devastación provocadas por los terremotos, la remoción de escombros constituye un primer paso fundamental para la recuperación. Una evaluación preliminar del Programa de las Naciones Unidas para el Desarrollo (PNUD) estima que los terremotos del 24 de junio generaron aproximadamente 1,2 millones de toneladas de escombros en las zonas más afectadas del estado La Guaira. Este análisis busca apoyar a las autoridades en la planificación de las labores de remoción de escombros y recuperación.

Este análisis busca apoyar a las autoridades en la planificación de las labores de remoción de escombros y recuperación. Para las familias y comunidades afectadas, despejar los escombros es el primer paso para restablecer el acceso, reabrir servicios esenciales e iniciar el proceso de recuperación. El análisis fue elaborado utilizando [RAPIDA]( la herramienta de evaluación rápida del PNUD, que combina imágenes satelitales, evaluaciones de daños en edificaciones basadas en inteligencia artificial, información sobre la ubicación y altura de los edificios, y conocimientos de ingeniería locales para estimar el volumen de escombros. Estas estimaciones están diseñadas para apoyar la planificación de las operaciones de recolección, transporte, almacenamiento temporal y disposición final de los escombros, facilitando un restablecimiento más rápido del acceso, la rehabilitación de los servicios esenciales y la transición hacia la recuperación y la reconstrucción.

chunks.title: Terremoto en Venezuela: CICR moviliza respuesta rápida en apoyo a la Cruz Roja Venezolana
sources: International Committee of the Red Cross
chunks.text: En los días posteriores a los terremotos del 24 de junio, la Cruz Roja Venezolana (CRV) se ha movilizado rápidamente para apoyar a las comunidades afectadas y a las autoridades nacionales. El CICR respaldó sus esfuerzos con asistencia de emergencia en áreas como agua, salud, gestión forense y bienestar de los detenidos. ## Suministro de agua Hasta ahora, el CICR ha donado **18.400 tabletas de purificación de agua** al Ministerio del Poder Popular para la Atención de las Aguas (MPPAA) de Venezuela, permitiendo el tratamiento de hasta **755.000 litros de agua** para su uso en hospitales. Según los estándares de Sphere, esta cantidad puede cubrir las necesidades diarias de agua de aproximadamente 50.000 personas a razón de 15 litros por persona al día. Además, se entregaron **21 cisternas de agua** a cuatro hospitales y dos refugios en La Guaira, la zona más afectada, proporcionando más de **297.000 litros de agua.** También se donaron **300 botellas de agua de veinte litros** al Ministerio de Aguas, así como **9.000 bolsas plásticas y 24 gafas de protección** al cuerpo de bomberos de Caracas.

Los ingenieros de agua y hábitat del CICR también brindaron apoyo técnico al equipo de agua, saneamiento e higiene de la Cruz Roja Venezolana, contribuyendo al diseño de instalaciones de duchas y sistemas eléctricos para el hospital de campaña en La Guaira. Asimismo, se adquirieron e instalaron ocho duchas, un generador eléctrico y **14 contenedores de residuos** para el hospital de campaña. ## Salud El CICR ha proporcionado **apoyo técnico y suministros médicos a la Cruz Roja Venezolana** y otros hospitales, incluyendo asistencia para establecer un hospital de campaña en La Guaira. El CICR también acompañó a los equipos de la CRV en evaluaciones de necesidades de RFL en cuatro hospitales de Caracas y en dos refugios, y apoyó la línea directa de la CRV, proporcionando asistencia directa a las personas que llamaban en busca de información. Además, se pusieron a disposición de la CRV **dos computadoras portátiles**, y se desplegaron sistemas de comunicación previamente donados por el CICR en La Guaira para apoyar la conectividad en la respuesta. También se realizó una evaluación de contactos familiares en La Guaira para mapear los refugios, identificar a las personas con necesidades de contacto familiar y evaluar la capacidad de respuesta de las autoridades locales y otras organizaciones. ### Apoyo continuo a las comunidades El CICR ha estado presente en Venezuela desde 1966, trabajando junto a las autoridades nacionales, la Cruz Roja Venezolana y la sociedad civil para abordar las consecuencias humanitarias de la violencia, la detención y el desplazamiento.

chunks.title: Venezuela earthquake: ICRC mobilizes rapid response in support of the Venezuelan Red Cross
sources: International Committee of the Red Cross
chunks.text: In the days following the 24 June earthquakes, the Venezuelan Red Cross (VRC) has moved quickly to support affected communities and national authorities. The ICRC supported their efforts, with emergency assistance spanning water, health, forensic management and detainee welfare. ## Water supply So far, the ICRC has donated **18,400 water purification tablets** to Venezuela's Ministry of Water (MPPAA), enabling the treatment of up to **755,000 litres of water** for use in hospitals. According to Sphere standards, this quantity can cover the daily water needs of approximately 50,000 people at 15 litres per person per day. **21 water cisterns** were also delivered to four hospitals and two shelters in La Guaira, the most affected area, providing more than **297,000 litres of water**. Additionally, **300 twenty-litre water bottles** were donated to the Ministry of Water, and **9,000 plastic bags** and **24 protective goggles** were donated to the Caracas fire service.

Additionally, **300 twenty-litre water bottles** were donated to the Ministry of Water, and **9,000 plastic bags** and **24 protective goggles** were donated to the Caracas fire service. ICRC water and habitat engineers also provided technical support to the Venezuelan Red Cross WASH team, contributing to the design of shower facilities and the electrical systems for the field hospital in La Guaira, and procured and installed eight showers and a generator for the field hospital, as well as **14 waste containers** for use at the facility. ## Health The ICRC has provided **technical support and medical supplies** to the Venezuelan Red Cross, including assistance in setting up a field hospital in La Guaira. On 26 June, the ICRC supported the transportation of a VRC water purification unit from Barquisimeto to La Guaira Stadium, where the field hospital is operating, so that it can provide clean water for both patients and the surrounding population. ## Forensic support The ICRC donated a total of **540 body bags** over 25 and 26 June to the National Forensic Medicine and Forensic Sciences Service (SENAMECF) at Bello Monte. On 27 June, a further **650 body bags** were distributed across three locations in La Guaira and an additional 150 body bags were donated to the Caracas fire service.

The ICRC also provided technical support to the VRC Disaster Risk Management Directorate for a rapid basic needs assessment and information management. ## Detainees and people deprived of liberty The ICRC intervened with prison authorities to facilitate Restoring Family Links (RFL) activities for people deprived of liberty. Information was shared to help them notify their families and re-establish contact with relatives from whom they had been separated.

In addition, **300 individual hygiene kits** – 150 for men and 150 for women – were donated to the Ministry of Prison Services (MPPSP). ## Restoring family links (RFL) and connectivity The ICRC has provided **10 mobile phones** to the Venezuelan Red Cross to support connectivity and family links activities and helped the VRC activate communication systems previously donated. Nine VRC volunteers received basic training on connectivity services and family links needs assessment. The ICRC also accompanied VRC teams conducting RFL needs assessments at four hospitals in Caracas and at two shelters, and supported the VRC hotline, providing direct assistance to people calling for information.

chunks.title: How MSF is responding to the earthquakes in Venezuela
chunks.text: ## What is the situation in Venezuela after the earthquakes? On 24 June 2026, two powerful [earthquakes]( struck Venezuela one after another. They have caused widespread damage, with the cities of La Guaira and Caracas particularly affected. At least 1,430 people have died and 3,230 have been injured, according to the authorities.[1]( Search and rescue operations are still ongoing, even as the initial emergency trauma phase is coming to an end.

chunks.text: They have caused widespread damage, with the cities of La Guaira and Caracas particularly affected. At least 1,430 people have died and 3,230 have been injured, according to the authorities.[1]( Search and rescue operations are still ongoing, even as the initial emergency trauma phase is coming to an end. Hospitals that were overwhelmed during the first days after the earthquakes are now receiving fewer patients. It is estimated that over 1,500 buildings were damaged, with most of them being residential. This has [displaced]( many families, who are now in need of shelter, [water and sanitation]( services, food, and medical care. ## How is MSF responding to the earthquakes in Venezuela?

chunks.title: Venezuela (República Bolivariana de): Respuesta a Terremotos - Reporte de Situación #2 (29 de junio de 2026)
chunks.text: Este segundo Informe de Situación presenta una actualización sobre el impacto de los terremotos del 24 de junio en la República Bolivariana de Venezuela y resume las actividades en curso y la respuesta planificada de la OIM en apoyo a las poblaciones afectadas y a los esfuerzos nacionales. **Aspectos destacados** Las cifras oficiales reportan al menos **1.719 personas fallecidas, 5.034 personas heridas, 15.866 personas severamente afectadas y 22.619 personas afectadas** tras los terremotos del 24 de junio. Al menos **855 edificaciones han sido afectadas**, incluyendo **189 colapsos totales**, mientras que el acceso a servicios básicos continúa interrumpido en varias zonas afectadas. Se han activado alojamientos temporales en los estados afectados, incluyendo sitios en **La Guaira, Caracas, Miranda y Aragua**. El **Polideportivo José María Vargas**, en Maiquetía, alberga a más de **1.200 personas** y se espera que reciba nuevas llegadas. **Actividades de la OIM** La OIM ha apoyado acciones de alojamiento, coordinación de sitios y servicios esenciales en alojamientos temporales, incluyendo la validación de información de **14 centros colectivos** que albergan a un estimado de **8.821 personas**, el mapeo y verificación de sitios de alojamiento temporal, y el establecimiento de servicios de salud y protección en el **Polideportivo José María Vargas**.

En este sitio, la OIM y las autoridades también han apoyado la instalación de servicios, incluyendo la entrega de **180 literas**. En salud, SMAPS, WASH, protección y datos, la OIM ha coordinado con las autoridades de salud de La Guaira para brindar servicios de salud de emergencia en sitios críticos de alojamiento temporal, incluyendo el **Polideportivo José María Vargas en Pariata** y el **Estadio César Nieves en Catia La Mar**. La OIM ha brindado servicios de salud de emergencia, atención primaria de salud a **220 personas**, coordinado capacidad de almacenamiento para medicamentos e insumos, desplegado **seis funcionarios de protección**, realizado evaluaciones de protección y mantenido el monitoreo de movilidad basado en DTM. **Respuesta planificada de la OIM** La respuesta planificada de la OIM continuará priorizando el alojamiento de emergencia y artículos de primera necesidad, la coordinación y gestión de sitios, salud y SMAPS, WASH, protección, y datos y evaluaciones de necesidades.

En salud, WASH, protección y datos, la OIM continuará brindando servicios de salud de emergencia, entregará insumos y equipos médicos esenciales, apoyará la atención de trauma y las rutas de derivación, y realizará evaluaciones de establecimientos de salud y apoyo operativo. La OIM también apoyará el acceso a agua de emergencia, la entrega de kits de higiene, artículos de higiene menstrual, puntos de lavado de manos, insumos para prevención y control de infecciones, saneamiento, gestión de residuos y promoción de higiene.

chunks.title: Venezuela (Bolivarian Republic of): Earthquake Response Situation Report #2 (29 June 2026)
chunks.text: This second Situation Report provides an updated overview of the impact of the 24 June earthquakes in the Bolivarian Republic of Venezuela and outlines IOM’s ongoing and planned response in support of affected populations and national efforts. **Highlights** Official figures report at least **1,719 fatalities, 5,034 injuries, 15,866 people severely affected and 22,619 people affected** following the 24 June earthquakes. At least **855 buildings have been affected**, including **189 total collapses**, while access to basic services remains disrupted in several affected areas. Temporary shelters have been activated in affected states, including sites in **La Guaira, Caracas, Miranda and Aragua**. The **Polideportivo José María Vargas in Maiquetía** is hosting more than **1,200 people** and is expected to receive additional arrivals. **IOM activities** IOM has supported shelter, site coordination and essential services in temporary accommodation sites, including the validation of information from **14 collective centres** hosting an estimated **8,821 people**, the mapping and verification of temporary accommodation sites, and the establishment of health and protection services at the **Polideportivo José María Vargas**.

chunks.title: Venezuela (Bolivarian Republic of): Earthquake Response Situation Report #2 (29 June 2026)
chunks.text: Temporary shelters have been activated in affected states, including sites in **La Guaira, Caracas, Miranda and Aragua**. The **Polideportivo José María Vargas in Maiquetía** is hosting more than **1,200 people** and is expected to receive additional arrivals. **IOM activities** IOM has supported shelter, site coordination and essential services in temporary accommodation sites, including the validation of information from **14 collective centres** hosting an estimated **8,821 people**, the mapping and verification of temporary accommodation sites, and the establishment of health and protection services at the **Polideportivo José María Vargas**. At this site, IOM and authorities have also supported the installation of services, including the delivery of **180 bunk beds**. In health, MHPSS, WASH, protection and data, IOM has coordinated with La Guaira health authorities to provide emergency health services in critical temporary accommodation sites, including **Polideportivo José María Vargas in Pariata** and **Estadio César Nieves in Catia La Mar**. IOM has delivered emergency health services, provided primary health care to **220 people**, coordinated storage capacity for medicines and supplies,has deployed **six protection staff**, conducted protection screening and maintained DTM-based mobility monitoring. **IOM planned response** IOM’s planned response will continue to prioritize emergency accomodation and core relief items, site coordination and management, health and MHPSS, WASH, protection, and data and needs assessments.

chunks.text: In health, MHPSS, WASH, protection and data, IOM has coordinated with La Guaira health authorities to provide emergency health services in critical temporary accommodation sites, including **Polideportivo José María Vargas in Pariata** and **Estadio César Nieves in Catia La Mar**. IOM has delivered emergency health services, provided primary health care to **220 people**, coordinated storage capacity for medicines and supplies,has deployed **six protection staff**, conducted protection screening and maintained DTM-based mobility monitoring. **IOM planned response** IOM’s planned response will continue to prioritize emergency accomodation and core relief items, site coordination and management, health and MHPSS, WASH, protection, and data and needs assessments. In site coordination, IOM will complete information gathering for remaining collective centres, strengthen monitoring, service mapping and referral mechanisms, provide technical support to authorities and site managers, support site improvements such as drainage, lighting and fire risk mitigation, and mobilize emergency shelter materials and core relief items. Across health, WASH, protection and data, IOM will continue emergency health services, deliver essential medical supplies and equipment, support trauma care and referral pathways, and provide health facility assessments and operational support. IOM will also support emergency water access, hygiene kits, menstrual hygiene items, handwashing points, infection prevention and control supplies, sanitation, waste management and hygiene promotion.
