The Venezuelan authorities have disclosed limited and uncorroborated information on the full extent of the human or material damage caused by the earthquakes. In this respect, Amnesty International calls on Venezuelan authorities to ensure the prompt, credible and regular disclosure of information regarding the extent of the damage, the number and characteristics of those killed or injured, the relief efforts being deployed, the assistance routes for those affected, and the contingency plan for searching for those missing, and rescuing and treating survivors. The organisation stresses that authorities must guarantee the right to life, personal integrity, and freedom while assisting the population. Access to information, freedom of the press, and freedom of expression have been severely restricted as a result of years of state-sponsored censorship, including the closure of dozens of media outlets, the blocking of social media platforms such as X, and the criminalization of journalists and human rights defenders.

In the context of the current humanitarian emergency, the organization stresses the critical importance of immediately lifting all undue restrictions on the press, social media platforms, and essential online communications channels. The potential impact of not doing so could be measured in lives lost and rights irreparably affected. Human rights and humanitarian NGOs are currently operating in a hugely restrictive environment as a result of a repressive legal architecture geared towards closing off civic space and targeting any form of perceived dissent.

Human rights and humanitarian NGOs are currently operating in a hugely restrictive environment as a result of a repressive legal architecture geared towards closing off civic space and targeting any form of perceived dissent. In order to offer an effective relief response plan, the Venezuelan authorities must immediately repeal the so-called Anti-NGO law and all other legal mechanisms that restrict, control and limit the lawful and necessary activities of these civil society organisations. Critically, Amnesty International highlights concerns over those who are in detention and their current situation in the aftermath of the earthquakes. While the organisation continues to call for the release all of those who are under politically motivated arbitrary detention, in the current context, Amnesty International also stresses the urgent call for humanitarian and human rights bodies and relatives of those detained to have access to all detention centres in order to verify the safety of all detainees and supply basic needs, including critical health care.

chunks.title: Terremoto en Venezuela Panorama de la situación (25 de junio de 2026)
chunks.text: **Panorama del terremoto** En la tarde-noche del 24 de junio de 2026, dos grandes terremotos sacudieron el norte de Venezuela con unos 40 segundos de diferencia: un sismo precursor de magnitud 7,2 y un sismo principal de magnitud 7,5. El USGS lo registra como el terremoto más fuerte en Venezuela en más de 125 años (USGS 24/06/2026, Al Jazeera 25/06/2026). Ambos sismos fueron superficiales y se produjeron en el sistema de fallas de Boconó-Morón-El Pilar, en el límite entre las placas del Caribe y Sudamericana; la profundidad del sismo principal, de unos 10 km, amplificó la sacudida en superficie, con una intensidad máxima cercana al grado IX (violento) de la escala de Mercalli modificada (MMI). Debe validarse con los informes de terreno, las evaluaciones oficiales y las priorizaciones de otros socios antes de comprometer recursos, en particular para las parroquias con puntuación alta alejadas del epicentro. Contexto previo a la crisis El terremoto ha golpeado a un país que ya acoge una de las crisis humanitarias más graves del hemisferio occidental y que se encuentra en plena y frágil transición política tras la salida del presidente Nicolás Maduro en enero de 2026. Antes de la catástrofe, se estimaba que entre 7,9 y 8,0 millones de personas, más de una cuarta parte de la población, tenían necesidades humanitarias, frente a un Plan de Respuesta Humanitaria PRH de 2026 que actualmente solo está financiado en torno al 23,2 % (ECHO consultado el 25/06/2026, HumVenezuela 31/03/2026, OCHA PNRH consultado el 25/06/2026 Indicador previo al terremoto (nacional) Cifra Personas con necesidades humanitarias 7,9–8,0 millones Población en situación de pobreza extrema 56 % Acceso limitado a un sistema sanitario fiable 70 % Acceso restringido al agua potable salubre 62 % Inseguridad alimentaria de moderada a grave 40 % Niños sin escolarización regular 30 % Viviendas que necesitan rehabilitación (nacional) 53,8 % Sarampión, difteria, Amenazas de enfermedades activas malaria Las estimaciones sectoriales nacionales de personas con necesidades PiN ponen de relieve que Venezuela ya afrontaba importantes retos humanitarios antes de cualquier impacto relacionado con el terremoto, lo que deja escasa capacidad para absorber una conmoción de gran escala. Antes del evento sísmico, se estimaba que 3,4 millones de personas (el 12,0 % de la población) necesitaban asistencia en seguridad alimentaria, lo que refleja problemas persistentes de acceso a los alimentos y de medios de vida.

El sector de la salud registró 5,5 millones de personas 19,3 % con necesidades por las limitaciones de acceso a la atención sanitaria, la disponibilidad de servicios y los medicamentos esenciales. Las necesidades eran especialmente acuciantes en el sector WASH, donde 11,6 millones de personas requerían apoyo para acceder a servicios de agua, saneamiento e higiene. La inseguridad alimentaria grave sigue aumentando, al pasar de 2,9 a 3,4 millones de personas afectadas entre 2024 y 2025, lo que indica una situación crítica de falta de medios de vida y una pobreza multidimensional más acusada, que no mejoraría con un aumento de los ingresos.

Desplazamiento Los dos terremotos provocaron desplazamientos a gran escala en varios estados del norte y el centro de Venezuela. Los residentes salieron a la calle mientras los edificios temblaban y permanecieron a la intemperie hasta bien entrada la noche, con cortes de electricidad, postes eléctricos derribados y escombros bloqueando las calles en las zonas afectadas (CBS News 25/06/2026. En varias ciudades se llevaron a cabo evacuaciones preventivas, y niños y familias se trasladaron a zonas abiertas mientras continúan las réplicas. Los terremotos se produjeron por la tarde-noche, cuando muchas personas regresaban a casa, lo que aumenta la preocupación de que haya personas atrapadas bajo estructuras derrumbadas (Save the Children 25/06/2026.

Varias de las prioridades señaladas a continuación se infieren de información temprana fragmentaria, de datos de vulnerabilidad preexistentes y de patrones consolidados de respuestas a terremotos comparables. Cada una de las necesidades señaladas recae sobre una población y un sistema ya sometidos a una fuerte presión: cerca de 8 millones de personas en Venezuela necesitaban apoyo humanitario antes de que se produjera el terremoto, frente a un plan de respuesta financiado solo al 23,2 % (OCHA 25/06/2026, NRC, 25/06/2026. Búsqueda y rescate (inmediato, para salvar vidas) ● Se mantienen operaciones de rescate activas en varios lugares con derrumbes confirmados de Caracas, entre ellos San Bernardino, El Paraíso, Altamira y Chacao, así como en La Guaira y en el estado de Falcón. El alcalde de Chacao confirmó que durante la noche los equipos de rescate aún podían oír a personas con vida bajo los escombros (CNN 25/06/2026. ● La Oficina de Coordinación de Asuntos Humanitarios de la ONU OCHA está coordinando el despliegue internacional de equipos de búsqueda y rescate urbano a través del Grupo Asesor Internacional de Operaciones de Búsqueda y Rescate INSARAG y ha enviado un equipo de respuesta rápida para reforzar su presencia en el país (OCHA 25/06/2026.

Retirada de escombros ● La presidenta encargada Rodríguez hizo un llamamiento público directo al sector privado para que aportara maquinaria pesada que ayudara en el rescate y la retirada de escombros, lo que indica que la capacidad de equipos del propio Gobierno es insuficiente para la magnitud de los derrumbes en varios estados (Yahoo News/AP 25/06/2026. Salud ● Con hospitales que se confirma están dañados y funcionan bajo presión, la carencia médica inmediata se centra en la cirugía de traumatismos, la atención de lesiones por aplastamiento, el tratamiento de heridas y el suministro de sangre. ● Direct Relief e International Medical Corps están movilizando material quirúrgico, antibióticos y kits de cura de heridas en respuesta a las solicitudes de los socios sanitarios locales (Direct Relief 25/06/2026, International Medical Corps 25/06/2026. ● La FICR señala además el apoyo psicosocial como una prioridad inmediata (FICR 25/06/2026. Esto recae sobre un sistema sanitario en el que aproximadamente el 70 % de la población ya carecía de acceso fiable a la atención antes del terremoto (ECHO Comisión Europea) 2026. ● Es probable que el mercado nacional de artículos esenciales, incluidos los suministros médicos, sea insuficiente para cubrir las necesidades a la escala actual, lo que hace críticas las importaciones internacionales (Al Jazeera 25/06/2026. Refugio y artículos no alimentarios ANA ● Con familias que no pueden regresar a viviendas derrumbadas o estructuralmente inseguras, y un riesgo continuo de réplicas que impide evaluar la integridad estructural de los edificios en pie (véase «Desplazamiento» y «Daños a los refugios»), la carencia operativa son los materiales de refugio de emergencia y los artículos domésticos esenciales para las familias desplazadas. La Organización Internacional para las Migraciones OIM confirmó que se está preparando para proporcionar ambos (OIM 25/06/2026. ● La evaluación estructural de los edificios en pie pero dañados es también una necesidad urgente: varios barrios de Caracas se han restringido parcialmente por el riesgo de nuevos derrumbes, y los residentes no pueden regresar con seguridad hasta que se inspeccionen los edificios (CNN 25/06/2026. ● Se desconoce la capacidad de las escuelas y los centros de acogida habilitados como refugios en relación con la necesidad real.

Es distinta de la estimación de fallecidos de PAGER anterior, que se guía por la intensidad de la sacudida y, en el caso de Venezuela, por una pronunciada función de pérdidas que concentra los fallecimientos en las parroquias de mayor intensidad.

chunks.text: Thousands of children at risk after powerful earthquakes strike Venezuela [EN/AR/ZH]

chunks.title: Thousands of children at risk after powerful earthquakes strike Venezuela [EN/AR/ZH]
chunks.text: **CARACAS/NEW YORK, 25 June 2026 –** An estimated 3.9 million children live in the areas affected by the powerful 7.5 and 7.2 magnitude earthquakes that struck Venezuela on 24 June, putting thousands of children and families at risk. The earthquakes affected communities in Caracas and the states of Aragua, Carabobo, Falcón, La Guaira, Miranda and surrounding areas. The most affected regions have seen dozens of buildings collapse, with children reportedly among the casualties. As authorities continue to assess the extent of the damage, reports indicate impacts on homes, public infrastructure and essential services, while communities remain at risk from possible aftershocks.

As authorities continue to assess the extent of the damage, reports indicate impacts on homes, public infrastructure and essential services, while communities remain at risk from possible aftershocks. “The images we are seeing from Venezuela and the stories we hear from colleagues on the ground are heartbreaking," said UNICEF Executive Director Catherine Russell. "Our thoughts are with the children and families who have lost loved ones and all of those whose lives have been upended. As the scale of the damage becomes clearer, children's safety, protection and well-being must remain at the center of the response.” Children are among the most vulnerable when disasters strike.

chunks.title: Good Neighbors Statement on the Venezuela Earthquake
chunks.text: Good Neighbors expresses its deepest sympathy to the communities affected by the devastating earthquakes that struck Venezuela on 24 June 2026. The earthquakes caused widespread destruction to homes, public infrastructure, and essential services, leaving thousands of families in urgent need of humanitarian assistance. Families have lost loved ones, their homes, and their sense of safety. Children, in particular, are facing fear, uncertainty, and significant disruption to their daily lives.

chunks.title: Good Neighbors Statement on the Venezuela Earthquake
chunks.text: Families have lost loved ones, their homes, and their sense of safety. Children, in particular, are facing fear, uncertainty, and significant disruption to their daily lives. As aftershocks continue, many families remain displaced, taking shelter in cars, makeshift tents, and other temporary accommodations without reliable access to electricity, safe drinking water, food, or protection services. In response to this crisis, Good Neighbors is preparing an emergency response to protect the safety, well-being, and dignity of children and their families. Initial support is expected to include emergency shelter and other essential relief items, while additional assistance will be determined based on ongoing needs assessments and operational feasibility.

chunks.title: Good Neighbors Statement on the Venezuela Earthquake
chunks.text: In response to this crisis, Good Neighbors is preparing an emergency response to protect the safety, well-being, and dignity of children and their families. Initial support is expected to include emergency shelter and other essential relief items, while additional assistance will be determined based on ongoing needs assessments and operational feasibility. We are closely monitoring the evolving situation through our humanitarian networks and local partners and coordinating with relevant authorities and humanitarian organizations to identify priority needs and provide timely, needs-based assistance in accordance with humanitarian principles. We stand ready to work alongside affected communities, national authorities, and humanitarian partners to support communities affected. We call upon the international community to stand in solidarity with the people of Venezuela by supporting timely, coordinated, and needs-based humanitarian assistance.

chunks.title: Good Neighbors Statement on the Venezuela Earthquake
chunks.text: We stand ready to work alongside affected communities, national authorities, and humanitarian partners to support communities affected. We call upon the international community to stand in solidarity with the people of Venezuela by supporting timely, coordinated, and needs-based humanitarian assistance. Together, we can help children, families, and communities recover, rebuild, and look toward the future with hope.

chunks.title: Trump Administration Leads a Robust Life-Saving Response to the Venezuelan Earthquakes
chunks.text: The United States is mobilizing an unprecedented, large-scale response to the devastating earthquakes that struck Venezuela on June 24, 2026. The Trump Administration has deployed a Disaster Assistance Response Team (DART) with more than 250 people, including three specialized Urban Search-and-Rescue (USAR) teams, which will conduct crucial life-saving operations. ## Life-Saving Support The Department activated three Urban Search-and-Rescue teams from Fairfax County, Virginia, Los Angeles County, California, and Miami-Dade County, Florida. The Fairfax County Fire and Rescue Department (USA-1), which deployed with 79 members and six canines, and the Los Angeles County Fire Department (USA-2), which will land soon, deployed with 74 members and six canines, after transportation from U.S. Air Force C-17 Globemaster aircraft. The Miami-Dade Fire Rescue (FLTF-1) is en route with 80 members and six canines and expected to arrive late Friday, June 26.

chunks.title: Trump Administration Leads a Robust Life-Saving Response to the Venezuelan Earthquakes
chunks.text: The Fairfax County Fire and Rescue Department (USA-1), which deployed with 79 members and six canines, and the Los Angeles County Fire Department (USA-2), which will land soon, deployed with 74 members and six canines, after transportation from U.S. Air Force C-17 Globemaster aircraft. The Miami-Dade Fire Rescue (FLTF-1) is en route with 80 members and six canines and expected to arrive late Friday, June 26. These USAR teams will conduct systematic search operations across collapsed structures, working to locate and extract survivors, and coordinate with local emergency responders and the Venezuelan interim government to prioritize the most heavily impacted areas. Together, they bring more than 200,000 pounds of specialized equipment. Each team is a multidisciplinary unit comprising firefighters trained in structural-collapse rescue, physicians and paramedics providing on-site emergency medical care, structural engineers assessing building integrity and collapse risk, and canine search specialists capable of locating survivors in rubble and debris fields.

All teams have prior international deployment experience. The Los Angeles and Fairfax teams have trained and deployed with the State Department and were activated in response to Hurricane Melissa in October 2025, where they surveyed affected areas in Jamaica, cleared debris to facilitate access, and assisted with the transportation of relief commodities to communities in need. ## SOUTHCOM Logistical Support The Department of State has requested the uniquely specialized capabilities of the U.S. military to support State-led disaster response and humanitarian assistance operations in Venezuela. The Department of War (DoW) is playing a crucial role in securing logistics for the response, including by leveraging military assets already positioned in the region and forward deploying personnel to accelerate the delivery of life-saving assistance. The DART and elements from U.S. Southern Command (SOUTHCOM) are working together to implement life-saving activities in close coordination with partners on the ground, drawing on SOUTHCOM’s regional presence to ensure rapid and sustained operational support. This includes: U.S. Air Force C-17s transporting Urban Search and Rescue teams and load-movement equipment to Caracas; U.S. Marine Corps MV-22 Ospreys conducting airfield assessments near the earthquake epicenter; U.S. Navy vessels USS Fort Lauderdale and USS Billings providing naval support in waters near Venezuela; U.S. Army CH-47 Chinooks deploying from Honduras to transport personnel and supplies; U.S. Space Force satellite imagery supporting damage assessment and prioritization of aid efforts. SOUTHCOM’s involvement reflects the deepening civil-military partnership with the Department’s Bureau of Disaster and Humanitarian Response (DHR), including the recent establishment of a U.S. humanitarian assistance hub in South Florida and the embedding of DHR disaster and humanitarian advisors at SOUTHCOM to strengthen coordination and technical expertise across the region. ## Restoring Connectivity: The U.S.-Starlink Partnership When disaster strikes, restoring connectivity is critical to saving lives.

SOUTHCOM’s involvement reflects the deepening civil-military partnership with the Department’s Bureau of Disaster and Humanitarian Response (DHR), including the recent establishment of a U.S. humanitarian assistance hub in South Florida and the embedding of DHR disaster and humanitarian advisors at SOUTHCOM to strengthen coordination and technical expertise across the region. ## Restoring Connectivity: The U.S.-Starlink Partnership When disaster strikes, restoring connectivity is critical to saving lives. The U.S. Government is working with Starlink to provide free satellite internet service to those affected by the Venezuelan earthquakes, rapidly deploying Starlink terminals to restore connectivity in the hardest-hit areas. This partnership is made possible by a two-year Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) signed between the U.S. Department of State and Starlink on June 11, 2026. The MOU leverages Starlink’s low-Earth orbit (LEO) satellite technology, an American innovation, to restore critical communications when crises and natural disasters damage infrastructure.

Under the agreement, DHR coordinates with Starlink to provide rapid connectivity to emergency responders, humanitarian organizations, and people in acute need. This response marks one of the first major activations of this partnership, demonstrating the real-world impact of the Trump Administration’s commitment to harnessing American innovation in service of humanitarian response. ## Humanitarian Assistance The Trump Administration is mobilizing $150 million in assistance to Venezuela, including: $50 million in new bilateral awards to partners including World Vision, Samaritan’s Purse, Catholic Relief Services, the International Organization for Migration, UNICEF, and the World Food Program; and $100 million contribution to the UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA) Venezuela pooled fund. ## Assisting Americans The Trump Administration has no higher priority than the safety and security of Americans. The Department of State is working tirelessly to provide consular assistance to U.S. citizens and their families in the affected areas.

chunks.title: After Venezuela Earthquakes, Direct Relief Supports Medical Deployment in Critical Response Window
chunks.text: ***Emergency grants to a search and rescue organization and medical brigade bolster immediate response, while Direct Relief advances wraparound medical support strategy.*** As an elite medical team deploys to Venezuela, Direct Relief is mobilizing an emergency grant to support their swift, effective response to Wednesday’s cataclysmic double earthquakes. The several days following a disaster are the most critical for medical intervention. Often working amid the rubble or in makeshift displacement centers, medical teams are able to save the lives of severely injured patients and keep emergent needs from spiraling into secondary crises. Medical Impact, a Mexico- and Colombia-based emergency response group with a storied history of responding in the immediate aftermath of natural disasters, sends mobile medical teams to global emergency settings from Guatemala to Gaza.

chunks.title: After Venezuela Earthquakes, Direct Relief Supports Medical Deployment in Critical Response Window
chunks.text: Often working amid the rubble or in makeshift displacement centers, medical teams are able to save the lives of severely injured patients and keep emergent needs from spiraling into secondary crises. Medical Impact, a Mexico- and Colombia-based emergency response group with a storied history of responding in the immediate aftermath of natural disasters, sends mobile medical teams to global emergency settings from Guatemala to Gaza. Equipped with field medic packs and emergency medicine caches – often provided by Direct Relief – they move through devastated terrain, treat physical trauma, prevent infection, help people purify water for drinking, and prevent people with conditions like asthma, diabetes, and HIV/AIDS from spiraling into medical crisis. An emergency grant “enables us to jump-start the response so we can start right away,” Dr. Giorgio Franyuti, Medical Impact’s executive director, told Direct Relief during a response to severe flooding in Mexico last October. Direct Relief also funded the deployment of a Spain-based search-and-rescue organization, [Bomberos Unidos Sin Fronteras]( with extensive [experience responding to this kind of devastation]( The next day’s activity will be critical in Northern Venezuela, where the earthquake toppled about 250 buildings, trapping survivors beneath.

chunks.title: Korean Government Provides Humanitarian Assistance to Venezuela Following Earthquake
sources: Government of the Republic of Korea
chunks.text: The government of the Republic of Korea has decided to provide Venezuela with USD5 million in humanitarian assistance through international organizations operating on the ground, in order to support the rapid response to and facilitate an early recovery from the recent devastating earthquake in the country that caused a loss of lives and damage to properties. \- According to the United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA)'s 2026 Global Humanitarian Overview, even prior to the earthquake, Venezuela already had 7.9 million people — more than 25% of its total population — in need of humanitarian assistance, owing to frequent natural disasters such as heavy rains and floodings, as well as political and economic instability including extreme inflation. The government of the Republic of Korea hopes that this assistance will contribute to a swift recovery of the affected areas and to an early restoration of normalcy to daily lives of affected communities.

chunks.title: Declaración de UNICEF sobre los terremotos de magnitud 7,5 y 7,2 en Venezuela
chunks.text: **CARACAS / PANAMA, 25 de junio de 2026** – UNICEF se solidariza con los niños, niñas, adolescentes y familias afectados por los terremotos de magnitud 7,5 y 7,2 que sacudieron Venezuela el 24 de junio de 2026. Los terremotos han afectado a comunidades de Caracas y de los estados Aragua, Carabobo, Falcón, La Guaira, Miranda y zonas cercanas. A medida que las evaluaciones oficiales de la situación evolucionan, se insta a las comunidades a mantenerse alerta ante posibles réplicas y a seguir las orientaciones de las autoridades. UNICEF está monitoreando de cerca la situación y enfatiza la importancia de garantizar la protección de los niños y las niñas afectados, asegurando que sus derechos permanezcan en el centro de la respuesta.

En las próximas horas y días, los niños y niñas necesitarán protección, apoyo psicosocial, agua segura, atención sanitaria y espacios seguros a medida que las comunidades se recuperan de la conmoción y la destrucción. UNICEF reafirma su compromiso de apoyar los esfuerzos nacionales para atender las necesidades de los niños afectados y sus familias, especialmente las de los más vulnerables. **Acerca de UNICEF** UNICEF es el organismo de las Naciones Unidas dedicado a la infancia, y su misión es proteger los derechos de todos los niños y niñas en todas partes, en especial los de los más desfavorecidos y de aquellos a los que resulta más difícil llegar. Trabajamos en más de 190 países y territorios, y hacemos lo que sea necesario para ayudarlos a sobrevivir, prosperar y desarrollar todo su potencial.

chunks.title: Venezuela Health Cluster: Earthquakes Situation Report #1 (25 June 2026) [EN/ES]
chunks.text: *English version follows* **Aspectos destacados y panorama del impacto** El 24 de junio de 2026, un "doblete sísmico" de alta intensidad, compuesto por dos grandes terremotos poco profundos (M7,2 y M7,5), sacudió el centro-norte de Venezuela en rápida sucesión, con epicentro cerca de Morón, en el eje Carabobo/Yaracuy. El Sistema Global de Alerta y Coordinación en Casos de Desastre (GDACS) emitió una Alerta Roja para el evento. La presidenta encargada, Delcy Rodríguez, declaró el estado de emergencia nacional, confirmando oficialmente 164 muertes y 971 heridos a nivel nacional, mientras que las autoridades del estado Miranda reportan, por separado, 20 muertes y 209 heridos adicionales en sus municipios. **Activación del sector salud y estado de los establecimientos críticos** La infraestructura de salud pública y privada ha sido plenamente activada en todo el país. Según el modelo preliminar de exposición de la OPS/OMS, hasta 91 hospitales de emergencia se encuentran en zonas de sacudida severa, incluidos 20 hospitales directamente expuestos a una intensidad de Mercalli VII o superior.

chunks.title: Venezuela Health Cluster: Earthquakes Situation Report #1 (25 June 2026) [EN/ES]
chunks.text: La presidenta encargada, Delcy Rodríguez, declaró el estado de emergencia nacional, confirmando oficialmente 164 muertes y 971 heridos a nivel nacional, mientras que las autoridades del estado Miranda reportan, por separado, 20 muertes y 209 heridos adicionales en sus municipios. **Activación del sector salud y estado de los establecimientos críticos** La infraestructura de salud pública y privada ha sido plenamente activada en todo el país. Según el modelo preliminar de exposición de la OPS/OMS, hasta 91 hospitales de emergencia se encuentran en zonas de sacudida severa, incluidos 20 hospitales directamente expuestos a una intensidad de Mercalli VII o superior. Se ha registrado una fuerte presión operativa, evacuaciones parciales y daños estructurales confirmados en múltiples establecimientos: **Hospital Domingo Luciani (El Llanito):** Evacuado por completo como medida preventiva; las evaluaciones técnicas de funcionalidad continúan en curso. **Hospital Dr. Francisco A. Rísquez (Cotiza):** Sufrió el colapso del ala del piso inferior, lo que provocó su evacuación y solicitudes urgentes de evaluación estructural. **Hospital Magallanes de Catia:** Varios pisos evacuados debido a roturas de tuberías y daños en la mampostería; se mantienen activas las solicitudes de carpas de emergencia y suministros de campo. **Hospital Victorino Santaella Ruiz (Los Teques):** Evacuado por las autoridades tras confirmarse daños estructurales en paredes internas y externas. **Otros establecimientos clave desbordados:** Se han reportado colapsos funcionales de las áreas de triaje de emergencia debido a la afluencia masiva de pacientes en el Hospital José María Vargas, el Hospital Pérez de León I y II, y el Hospital Vargas de La Guaira. **Logística, entrada humanitaria y redes ciudadanas** Los servicios públicos críticos (electricidad, agua, gas médico y telecomunicaciones) están sufriendo interrupciones severas, lo que amenaza la continuidad de la atención hospitalaria. Si bien el Aeropuerto Internacional Simón Bolívar (Maiquetía) sufrió daños en su infraestructura, ha sido reabierto exclusivamente para operaciones humanitarias y de respuesta.

chunks.title: Venezuela Health Cluster: Earthquakes Situation Report #1 (25 June 2026) [EN/ES]
chunks.text: Acting President Delcy Rodríguez declared a national state of emergency, officially confirming **164 deaths and 971 injuries** nationwide , while Miranda State authorities separately report an additional **20 deaths and 209 injuries** across its municipalities. **Health Sector Activation & Critical Facility Status** The public and private healthcare infrastructure has been fully activated across the country. According to preliminary PAHO/WHO exposure modelling, up to 91 emergency hospitals are located in severe shaking areas, including 20 hospitals directly exposed to Mercalli intensity VII or higher. Severe operational strain, partial evacuations, and confirmed structural damages have been registered across multiple facilities: **Hospital Domingo Luciani (El Llanito):** Fully evacuated as a preventative measure; technical functionality evaluations remain ongoing. **Hospital Dr. Francisco A. Rísquez (Cotiza):** Suffered a lower floor wing collapse, leading to an evacuation and urgent requests for structural assessments. **Hospital Magallanes de Catia:** Multiple floors evacuated due to ruptured pipelines and masonry damage; requests for emergency tents and field supplies are active. **Hospital Victorino Santaella Ruiz (Los Teques):** Evacuated by authorities following confirmed structural damage to internal and external walls. **Other Key Overwhelmed Facilities:** Functional collapses of emergency triage areas due to massive patient influxes have been reported at *Hospital José María Vargas*, *Hospital Pérez de León I and II*, and *Hospital Vargas de La Guaira*. **Logistics, Humanitarian Entry & Citizen Networks** Critical utility lifelines (electricity, water, medical gas, and telecommunications) are experiencing severe disruptions, threatening the continuity of hospital care. While Simón Bolívar International Airport (Maiquetía) sustained infrastructure damage, it has been reopened strictly for humanitarian and response operations.

Priority Health Risks and Needs Pre-existing Health Risks (Aggravated by the Earthquake) Venezuela's protracted humanitarian crisis had severely weakened the health system prior to the earthquake, including a 37% shortage index for hospital emergency supplies (September 2024), critical staffing gaps, limited access to diagnostic and imaging services, and the inability of most hospitals to sustain essential services — water, electricity and medical gases — for more than 72 hours during outages. From an epidemiological perspective, Venezuela faces re-emergence of vaccine-preventable diseases (measles, diphtheria, pertussis) and persistent vector-borne disease burden (dengue, chikungunya, Zika, Oropouche, malaria, yellow fever).

Panorama general de la situación El 24 de junio de 2026, a las 18:04 hora local, dos grandes terremotos sacudieron el centro-norte de Venezuela en rápida sucesión. Según el Servicio Geológico de los Estados Unidos (USGS), el primer evento registró una magnitud de 7,1–7,2 con epicentro al oeste de Morón (costa caribeña), a una profundidad aproximada de 13 km. Aproximadamente un minuto después, ocurrió un segundo terremoto de magnitud 7,5 al suroeste de Morón, a una profundidad aproximada de 10 km.

Riesgos y necesidades de salud prioritarios Riesgos de salud preexistentes (agravados por el terremoto) La prolongada crisis humanitaria de Venezuela había debilitado gravemente el sistema de salud antes del terremoto, incluyendo un índice de desabastecimiento del 37 % en insumos de emergencia hospitalaria (septiembre de 2024), brechas críticas de personal, acceso limitado a servicios de diagnóstico e imagenología, y la incapacidad de la mayoría de los hospitales para sostener servicios esenciales — agua, electricidad y gases médicos — durante más de 72 horas en caso de interrupciones. Desde una perspectiva epidemiológica, Venezuela enfrenta la reaparición de enfermedades prevenibles por vacunación (sarampión, difteria, tos ferina) y una carga persistente de enfermedades transmitidas por vectores (dengue, chikunguña, zika, Oropouche, malaria, fiebre amarilla). Es probable que el terremoto genere demandas adicionales de insumos médicos de emergencia, atención de trauma, capacidad de evaluación de establecimientos de salud y coordinación operativa.

chunks.title: UNICEF statement on 7.5 and 7.2 magnitude earthquakes in Venezuela
chunks.text: **CARACAS / PANAMA 25 June 2026 –** UNICEF stands in solidarity with the children and families affected by the 7.5 and 7.2 magnitude earthquakes that struck Venezuela on 24 June 2026. The earthquakes have affected communities in Caracas and the states of Aragua, Carabobo, Falcón, La Guaira, Miranda and nearby areas. As official situation assessments evolve, communities are urged to remain alert for possible aftershocks and follow official guidance. UNICEF is monitoring the situation closely and emphasizes the importance of ensuring that affected children are protected and that their rights remain at the centre of the response.

chunks.title: UNICEF statement on 7.5 and 7.2 magnitude earthquakes in Venezuela
chunks.text: As official situation assessments evolve, communities are urged to remain alert for possible aftershocks and follow official guidance. UNICEF is monitoring the situation closely and emphasizes the importance of ensuring that affected children are protected and that their rights remain at the centre of the response. In the hours and days ahead, children will need protection, psychosocial support, safe water, healthcare and safe spaces as communities recover from the shock and destruction. UNICEF is committed to supporting national efforts to address the needs of affected children and their families, particularly the most vulnerable. **About UNICEF** UNICEF, the United Nations agency for children, works to protect the rights of every child, everywhere, especially the most disadvantaged children and in the toughest places to reach. Across more than 190 countries and territories, we do whatever it takes to help children survive, thrive, and fulfil their potential.

La ocurrencia de múltiples réplicas (más de 130 según datos oficiales) mantiene condiciones de riesgo elevado. Los dos eventos principales ocurrieron con apenas 39–40 segundos de diferencia, con epicentro frente a la costa centro-norte, a unos 28–30 km al noroeste de Montalbán (estado Carabobo). La respuesta gubernamental está centrada en operaciones de búsqueda y rescate, atención médica de emergencia y evaluación de daños.

La respuesta gubernamental está centrada en operaciones de búsqueda y rescate, atención médica de emergencia y evaluación de daños. El impacto ha sido severo y generalizado, afectando infraestructura crítica, servicios públicos y viviendas en varios estados, con mayor concentración en Distrito Capital, La Guaira, Miranda, Carabobo y Yaracuy. Caracas registró sacudidas prolongadas (60 segundos), resultando en pánico generalizado, evacuaciones y daños estructurales significativos en edificaciones. El estado La Guaira ha sido identificado como el epicentro del impacto más severo, con reportes de múltiples colapsos y condiciones calificadas como zona de desastre, donde continúan operaciones intensivas de rescate.

chunks.title: Earthquakes in Venezuela: Situation Report #2 (25 June 2026, Time: 3:00 pm)
sources: UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs
chunks.text: **Situation Report #2** **Earthquakes in Venezuela** **25 June 2026** **Time: 3:00 pm** **Highlights** Two consecutive earthquakes of magnitude 7.2 and 7.5 recorded at around 18:00 on Wednesday 24 June, with more than 130 aftershocks. 211 people dead and 1261 injured (provisional figure), according to authorities as of the afternoon of Thursday, June 25. 250 buildings were affected or suffered total loss, particularly in La Guaira, according to official information. La Guaira state identified as the most affected, with multiple collapsed buildings. Significant structural damage in Caracas, including partial collapses and mass evacuations. Activation of the State of Emergency and the response General Staff.

chunks.title: Earthquakes in Venezuela: Situation Report #2 (25 June 2026, Time: 3:00 pm)
sources: UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs
chunks.text: Significant structural damage in Caracas, including partial collapses and mass evacuations. Activation of the State of Emergency and the response General Staff. International rescue teams on the way. **General situation** Venezuela is facing a national emergency following two consecutive high-magnitude earthquakes in the north-central region of the country on 24 June at around 18:00 (local time). The first event (M7.2) was followed by a second of greater intensity (up to M7.5), which significantly amplified the surface impact. The occurrence of multiple aftershocks (more than 130 aftershocks, according to official information.) maintains elevated risk conditions.

chunks.title: Earthquakes in Venezuela: Situation Report #2 (25 June 2026, Time: 3:00 pm)
sources: UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs
chunks.text: The first event (M7.2) was followed by a second of greater intensity (up to M7.5), which significantly amplified the surface impact. The occurrence of multiple aftershocks (more than 130 aftershocks, according to official information.) maintains elevated risk conditions. The two main events occurred just 39–40 seconds apart, with an epicenter off the central-northern coast, about 28–30 km northwest of Montalbán (Carabobo state). The governmental response is focused on search-and-rescue operations, emergency medical care and damage assessment. The impact has been severe and widespread, affecting critical infrastructure, public services and housing in several states, with the greatest concentration in the Capital District, La Guaira, Miranda, Carabobo and Yaracuy.

chunks.title: Earthquakes in Venezuela: Situation Report #2 (25 June 2026, Time: 3:00 pm)

The impact has been severe and widespread, affecting critical infrastructure, public services and housing in several states, with the greatest concentration in the Capital District, La Guaira, Miranda, Carabobo and Yaracuy. Caracas experienced prolonged shaking (60 seconds), resulting in widespread panic, evacuations and significant structural damage to buildings. La Guaira state has been identified as the epicentre of the most severe impact, with reports of multiple collapses and conditions classified as a disaster zone, where intensive rescue operations continue. The provisional official toll reports 211 people dead and 1261 injured.

chunks.title: Situation Report No.1: Earthquakes in Venezuela (M7.2 and M7.5), June 25, 2026
chunks.text: **HIGHLIGHTS** On 24 June 2026, two consecutive earthquakes (M7.2 and M7.5) struck Yaracuy state in north-central Venezuela with ~3.9 million people exposed to severe shaking. The earthquake was felt across several states, including Miranda, Aragua, Yaracuy, Lara, Mérida, Falcón, Carabobo, La Guaira and the Capital District. La Guaira may be among the worst affected –with multiple collapsed buildings, ongoing search and rescue, and a disaster-area declaration – while collapsed buildings and damaged infrastructure are also reported in parts of Caracas and Miranda. Assessments are still ongoing Venezuela's Acting President, Delcy Rodríguez, has declared a state of emergency and reported on Thursday that 164 deaths and 971 injuries had been registered following the two major earthquakes.

Assessments are still ongoing Venezuela's Acting President, Delcy Rodríguez, has declared a state of emergency and reported on Thursday that 164 deaths and 971 injuries had been registered following the two major earthquakes. The public and private health networks have reportedly been mobilized to provide immediate care to injured people (including 20 public and private health facilities in Gran Caracas). Reported disruptions to electricity, water, domestic gas, transport systems and telecommunications in affected areas may further affect health service continuity, emergency referrals, hospital operations, ambulance dispatch, referral pathways and coordination. The Simon Bolivar International Airport was reportedly seriously affected and is currently closed.

Priority health risks and needs Health risks: Venezuela’s protracted humanitarian crisis has severely weakened the health system, driving widespread medicine shortages – reflected in a 37% shortage index for hospital emergency supplies as of September 2024 – alongside deteriorating service quality, critical staffing gaps and limited access to diagnostic and imaging services. chunks.text: Priority health risks and needs Health risks: Venezuela’s protracted humanitarian crisis has severely weakened the health system, driving widespread medicine shortages – reflected in a 37% shortage index for hospital emergency supplies as of September 2024 – alongside deteriorating service quality, critical staffing gaps and limited access to diagnostic and imaging services. Many hospitals cannot sustain essential services—water, power, and medical gas—for 72 hours during outages, and no contingency plans have been reported. From an epidemiological perspective, Venezuela faces substantial public health threats, including the re-emergence of vaccine-preventable diseases such as measles, diphtheria, and pertussis, driven by insufficient immunization coverage. In addition, vector-borne diseases—including dengue, chikungunya, Zika, Oropouche, malaria, and yellow fever—remain significant and persistent health challenges. Given the pre-existing fragility of the health system and the protracted humanitarian emergency in Venezuela, the earthquake is likely to drive additional requests for support, including emergency medical supplies, trauma care, health facility assessments, and operational coordination.

sources: UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs
chunks.text: **Terremotos en Venezuela** **25 de junio de 2026** **Hora: 03:00 am** **Destacados** Dos sismos consecutivos de magnitud 7.2 y 7.5 registrados alrededor de las 18:00 H, con más de 20 réplicas. 32 personas fallecidas (preliminar) y más de 700 heridos, según autoridades. Estado La Guaira identificado como el más afectado, con múltiples edificaciones colapsadas. Daños estructurales significativos en Caracas, incluyendo colapsos parciales y evacuaciones masivas. Aeropuerto de Maiquetía cerrado, Metro y ferrocarril suspendidos.

chunks.title: Terremotos en Venezuela: Reporte de situación #1 (25 de junio de 2026, Hora: 03:00 am)
sources: UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs
chunks.text: Daños estructurales significativos en Caracas, incluyendo colapsos parciales y evacuaciones masivas. Aeropuerto de Maiquetía cerrado, Metro y ferrocarril suspendidos. Activación del Estado de Emergencia y del Estado Mayor de respuesta. Equipos internacionales de rescate en camino. **Situación general** Venezuela enfrenta una emergencia nacional tras la ocurrencia de dos sismos consecutivos de gran magnitud en la región centro-norte del país el 24 de junio alrededor de las 18:00 (hora local). El primer evento (M7.2) fue seguido por un segundo de mayor intensidad (hasta M7.5), lo que amplificó significativamente el impacto en superficie.

chunks.title: Terremotos en Venezuela: Reporte de situación #1 (25 de junio de 2026, Hora: 03:00 am)
sources: UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs
chunks.text: Equipos internacionales de rescate en camino. **Situación general** Venezuela enfrenta una emergencia nacional tras la ocurrencia de dos sismos consecutivos de gran magnitud en la región centro-norte del país el 24 de junio alrededor de las 18:00 (hora local). El primer evento (M7.2) fue seguido por un segundo de mayor intensidad (hasta M7.5), lo que amplificó significativamente el impacto en superficie. La ocurrencia de múltiples réplicas (más de 20) mantiene condiciones de riesgo elevado. La respuesta gubernamental está centrada en operaciones de búsqueda y rescate, atención médica de emergencia y evaluación de daños. El impacto ha sido severo y generalizado, afectando infraestructura crítica, servicios públicos y viviendas en varios estados, con mayor concentración en Distrito Capital, La Guaira, Miranda, Carabobo y Yaracuy.

chunks.title: Terremotos en Venezuela: Reporte de situación #1 (25 de junio de 2026, Hora: 03:00 am)
sources: UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs
chunks.text: La respuesta gubernamental está centrada en operaciones de búsqueda y rescate, atención médica de emergencia y evaluación de daños. El impacto ha sido severo y generalizado, afectando infraestructura crítica, servicios públicos y viviendas en varios estados, con mayor concentración en Distrito Capital, La Guaira, Miranda, Carabobo y Yaracuy. Caracas registró sacudidas prolongadas (60 segundos), resultando en pánico generalizado, evacuaciones y daños estructurales significativos en edificaciones. El estado La Guaira ha sido identificado como el epicentro del impacto más severo, con reportes de colapsos múltiples y condiciones calificadas como zona de desastre, donde continúan operaciones intensivas de rescate. El balance preliminar reporta 32 personas fallecidas y más de 700 heridas, con cifras sujetas a actualización conforme avanzan las labores en estructuras colapsadas.

chunks.title: Venezuela Earthquake Situation Overview (25 June, 2026)
chunks.text: On 24 June 2026, northern Venezuela was struck by two powerful earthquakes approximately 40 seconds apart - a magnitude 7.2 foreshock followed by a magnitude 7.5 mainshock, making it the country's strongest recorded earthquake in more than 125 years. The shallow earthquakes generated violent ground shaking across northern Venezuela, causing widespread damage to homes, health facilities, schools, transport infrastructure, and essential services. As of 25 June, at least 164 people have been confirmed dead and 971 injured, although casualty figures are expected to rise as search and rescue operations continue and assessments reach previously inaccessible areas. This report provides a consolidated overview of the evolving humanitarian situation, including the geographic extent of the earthquake and an assessment of the most affected states, municipalities, and parishes.

chunks.title: Venezuela Earthquake Situation Overview (25 June, 2026)
chunks.text: As of 25 June, at least 164 people have been confirmed dead and 971 injured, although casualty figures are expected to rise as search and rescue operations continue and assessments reach previously inaccessible areas. This report provides a consolidated overview of the evolving humanitarian situation, including the geographic extent of the earthquake and an assessment of the most affected states, municipalities, and parishes. It also analyses the humanitarian impacts in the context of Venezuela's pre-existing vulnerabilities, which are likely to compound the effects of the disaster and increase humanitarian needs. Drawing on available information, the report identifies priority humanitarian needs across key sectors, highlights the populations and locations facing the greatest risks, and outlines key response considerations and likely operational priorities to support emergency response, humanitarian coordination, and the transition towards early recovery. The methodology utilized in this report has been jointly developed with GiveDirectly.

chunks.text: Estimation method and data sources..18 Earthquake overview On the evening of 24 June 2026, two major earthquakes struck northern Venezuela about 40 seconds apart: a magnitude 7.2 foreshock and a magnitude 7.5 mainshock. The USGS records it as the strongest earthquake in Venezuela in more than 125 years (USGS 24/06/2026, Al Jazeera 25/06/2026. Both shocks were shallow on the Boconó-Morón-El Pilar fault system, at the Caribbean and South American plate boundary; the mainshockʼs depth of about 10 km amplified surface shaking, with peak intensity approaching MMI 9 (violent). Shaking was felt across northern Venezuela and into Colombia (USGS 24/06/2026, Al Jazeera 25/06/2026. chunks.title: Venezuela Earthquake Situation Overview (25 June, 2026)
chunks.text: The table shows two different measures side by side, and they answer different questions. The relevance score, a 0 to 100 measure in the dataset, estimates how many likely-deprived people felt damaging shaking: the population exposed at MMI VI or above, weighted by deprivation. It counts exposure above the VI threshold and does not scale with how intense the shaking was. Estimated fatalities come from a separate model USGS PAGER driven by shaking intensity, which for Venezuela rises steeply, so deaths concentrate in the highest-intensity parishes near the epicentre. The two diverge by design: relevance shows where many vulnerable people were exposed, PAGER shows where deaths are most likely.

Prior to the seismic event, an estimated 3.4 million people 12.0% of the population) required food security assistance, reflecting persistent challenges related to food access and livelihoods. The health sector recorded 5.5 million people 19.3% in need due to constraints on healthcare access, service availability, and essential medicines. Needs were particularly acute in the WASH sector, where 11.6 million people required support to access safe water, sanitation, and hygiene services. Severe food insecurity continues to increase, going from 2.9 to 3.4 million people affected between 2024 and 2025, which indicates a critical situation of lack of livelihoods and a more pronounced multidimensional poverty, which would not improve with income increases.

chunks.text: Needs were particularly acute in the WASH sector, where 11.6 million people required support to access safe water, sanitation, and hygiene services. Severe food insecurity continues to increase, going from 2.9 to 3.4 million people affected between 2024 and 2025, which indicates a critical situation of lack of livelihoods and a more pronounced multidimensional poverty, which would not improve with income increases. In addition, 2.1 million children and adolescents remained out of school - half are between 0 to 5 years old, highlighting longstanding barriers to safe and continuous learning. Collectively, these figures illustrate that the earthquake struck a population with substantial pre-existing humanitarian needs, increasing the likelihood that disruptions to infrastructure and essential services will translate into disproportionately severe impacts and place additional strain on already overstretched response capacities (ECHO assessed 25/06/2026, HumVenezuela 31/03/2026, OCHA HNRP assessed 25/06/2026. Displacement The twin earthquakes triggered large-scale displacement across multiple states in northern and central Venezuela.

chunks.title: Venezuela Earthquake Situation Overview (25 June, 2026)
chunks.text: No government or UN agency has published a total displaced persons count as of this report. Displacement The twin earthquakes triggered large-scale displacement across multiple states in northern and central Venezuela. Residents moved into the streets as buildings shook and remained outdoors well after nightfall, with power cuts, toppled electric poles, and debris blocking streets across affected areas (CBS News 25/06/2026. Preventative evacuations were carried out in several cities, with children and families moving into open areas as aftershocks continue. The earthquakes struck during the evening when many people were returning home, increasing concerns that individuals may be trapped beneath collapsed structures (Save the Children 25/06/2026.

chunks.title: Venezuela Earthquake Situation Overview (25 June, 2026)
chunks.text: Preventative evacuations were carried out in several cities, with children and families moving into open areas as aftershocks continue. The earthquakes struck during the evening when many people were returning home, increasing concerns that individuals may be trapped beneath collapsed structures (Save the Children 25/06/2026. Displacement by Location Spontaneous displacement was confirmed across several locations: ● La Guaira: the coastal state north of Caracas was the worst-affected area and was declared a disaster zone, with extensive building collapse reported in Macuto and Catia La Mar (CNN, 25/06/2026. No formal shelter count has been published for the state. ● Falcón state: Governor Víctor Clark confirmed 32 people hospitalized and 15 still trapped hours after the quake (NBC Miami, 25/06/2026. ● Caracas: more than 500 emergency workers were deployed to collapsed and damaged buildings in Chacao municipality alone, gas supply was cut, and large areas lost power (CNN, 25/06/2026. ● Brazil (cross-border): Buildings were also evacuated in Brazilʼs Amazon cities of Manaus, Belém, and Macapá as tremors were felt, though no damage or injuries were reported there (NBC Miami, 25/06/2026. Damage to Shelter ● National authorities activated search-and-rescue operations and set up reception centres for people affected, while hospitals received the injured (IFRC 25/06/2026. ● Venezuelaʼs Ministry of Education announced late Wednesday that some schools would be used as shelters and donation centres, though this sits in tension with the governmentʼs simultaneous multi-day school closure order, indicating shelter capacity planning is still being established (CBS News 25/06/2026. ● The Red Cross confirmed its nationwide hospital and clinic network was operational and that volunteers were supporting relief efforts, with priorities centered on survivor rescue, emergency shelter, healthcare, and safe water and sanitation access (CNN 25/06/2026.

Relevance score. The relevance score answers a specific question: how many likely-deprived people felt damaging shaking. It takes the population exposed to MMI VI or above, a fixed threshold, so it counts exposure above VI rather than scaling with how intense the shaking was, and weights it by a deprivation score blending NASA SEDAC's Gridded Relative Deprivation Index with OPHI's Multidimensional Poverty Index.

chunks.text: The relevance score answers a specific question: how many likely-deprived people felt damaging shaking. It takes the population exposed to MMI VI or above, a fixed threshold, so it counts exposure above VI rather than scaling with how intense the shaking was, and weights it by a deprivation score blending NASA SEDAC's Gridded Relative Deprivation Index with OPHI's Multidimensional Poverty Index. The vulnerability-weighted population, the affected population multiplied by one plus that deprivation score, is rescaled to a 0 to 100 score within the event. It is distinct from the PAGER fatality estimate above, which is driven by shaking intensity and, for Venezuela, by a steep loss function that concentrates deaths in the highest-intensity parishes. The relevance score is an initial version that the modelling team intends to refine, including treating intensity continuously rather than at a fixed VI threshold; it is indicative and should be validated against field and official sources.

sources: UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs
chunks.text: **Earthquakes in Venezuela** **June 25, 2026** **Time: 3:00 am** **Highlights** Two consecutive earthquakes of approximately M7.2 and M7.5 occurred around 18:00 local time, followed by more than 20 aftershocks. 32 fatalities (preliminary) and over 700 injured, according to authorities. La Guaira State identified as the most affected, with multiple buildings collapsed. Significant structural damage in Caracas, including partial collapses and mass evacuations. Maiquetía International Airport closed; Metro and rail services suspended.

chunks.title: Earthquakes in Venezuela: Situation Report #1 (June 25, 2026, Time: 3:00 am)
sources: UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs
chunks.text: Significant structural damage in Caracas, including partial collapses and mass evacuations. Maiquetía International Airport closed; Metro and rail services suspended. chunks.title: Venezuela: IRC launches emergency response in wake of devastating twin earthquakes
chunks.text: **Thousands of people face urgent humanitarian needs following powerful twin earthquakes measuring 7.2 and 7.5 on the Richter scale** Caracas, Venezuela, June 25, 2026 — Two powerful earthquakes have killed at least 164 people and injured nearly 1,000 across Venezuela, leaving thousands more in urgent need of emergency assistance. The International Rescue Committee (IRC) is mobilizing an initial emergency response to reach those in need, including the distribution of essential relief items and emergency medical supplies to frontline workers in the most affected areas. As the situation develops, the IRC will assess further needs across affected communities. The earthquakes have compounded an already severe humanitarian situation in Venezuela, where years of economic collapse and displacement have left communities with little capacity to absorb a disaster of this scale.

chunks.title: Venezuela: IRC launches emergency response in wake of devastating twin earthquakes
chunks.text: As the situation develops, the IRC will assess further needs across affected communities. The earthquakes have compounded an already severe humanitarian situation in Venezuela, where years of economic collapse and displacement have left communities with little capacity to absorb a disaster of this scale. Many families impacted by the earthquakes were already struggling to meet their most basic needs. With national services under significant strain, essential rescue and recovery efforts may take weeks if not months. *"What we are seeing is catastrophic,"* **said Nicole Kast, IRC Venezuela Country Director.** *"People have lost everything in a matter of seconds, and the need for immediate support is overwhelming. In some of the hardest-hit areas, damaged infrastructure and limited civil response capacity mean people may be trapped and unable to reach safety or be reached by those trying to help.

chunks.text: With national services under significant strain, essential rescue and recovery efforts may take weeks if not months. *"What we are seeing is catastrophic,"* **said Nicole Kast, IRC Venezuela Country Director.** *"People have lost everything in a matter of seconds, and the need for immediate support is overwhelming. In some of the hardest-hit areas, damaged infrastructure and limited civil response capacity mean people may be trapped and unable to reach safety or be reached by those trying to help. We are working to get supplies to frontline workers as fast as possible so that lives can be saved."* Venezuela was already facing a protracted humanitarian crisis before these earthquakes struck with nearly 8 million people in need of urgent humanitarian assistance and millions of people living in poverty with limited access to basic services. The IRC has been working in Venezuela since 2021, providing health, protection, and emergency support to vulnerable populations. Our teams work with local partners to address urgent health, nutrition, protection, education, food security, and livelihood needs for Venezuelans inside Venezuela and across the border in Colombia. ## **Media contacts** Sylvan Foley ** ** IRC Global Communications ** **

chunks.title: Declaración del portavoz de la OIM sobre los terremotos en Venezuela
chunks.text: **Ginebra, 25 de junio de 2026** – La Organización Internacional para las Migraciones (OIM) expresa su profunda consternación ante los devastadores terremotos que han afectado a Venezuela, causando destrucción, numerosas víctimas mortales y heridos, y afectando a numerosas familias y comunidades. Nuestros pensamientos están con quienes han perdido a sus seres queridos, han resultado heridos o han perdido sus hogares y medios de vida. En este difícil momento, expresamos nuestra solidaridad con el pueblo de Venezuela y con los equipos de primera respuesta que trabajan incansablemente para salvar vidas y asistir a las personas afectadas. Muchas personas se encuentran desplazadas o requieren asistencia urgente.

chunks.title: Declaración del portavoz de la OIM sobre los terremotos en Venezuela
chunks.text: En este difícil momento, expresamos nuestra solidaridad con el pueblo de Venezuela y con los equipos de primera respuesta que trabajan incansablemente para salvar vidas y asistir a las personas afectadas. Muchas personas se encuentran desplazadas o requieren asistencia urgente. Los equipos de la OIM están evaluando la situación y en coordinación estrecha estrechamente con las autoridades nacionales y locales, los asociados de las Naciones Unidas y las organizaciones humanitarias para determinar las necesidades más urgentes y apoyar una respuesta rápida. Como parte de sus esfuerzos de preparación, la OIM se está movilizando para brindar asistencia vital, incluidos servicios de alojamiento de emergencia, agua, saneamiento e higiene, así como atención de salud y artículos no alimentarios esenciales para las familias afectadas, al tiempo que apoya los esfuerzos para garantizar que las familias desplazadas reciban la protección y la asistencia que necesitan. La magnitud de esta crisis exige una acción rápida y colectiva.

chunks.title: M 7.5 - 28 km SE of Yumare, Venezuela | Shake MMI Impact Zones
chunks.text: Two major earthquakes struck near Yumare, Venezuela on 24 June — an M 7.2 followed one minute later by an M 7.5, both triggering red USGS alerts. iMMAP's rapid impact analysis, combining USGS ShakeMap intensity data with WorldPop 2026 population figures, shows the scale of potential exposure: → ~590,000 people in severe to violent shaking zones (MMI VII+) across both events → 4.8 million exposed to strong shaking (VI) from the M 7.5 alone → Over 16 million people within the total earthquake footprint The shaking footprint of the stronger, shallower M 7.5 event extends toward the Valencia–Caracas urban corridor — one of Venezuela's most densely populated areas — placing significant urban populations within high-intensity zones. The sequential nature of these events compounds the challenge: cumulative structural damage, disrupted access routes, and overlapping needs will shape what an effective response looks like in the hours and days ahead.

chunks.text: The European Union conveys its condolences to the families and loved ones of the victims of the devastating earthquakes that struck Venezuela. At this difficult moment, the European Union expresses its solidarity with the people of Venezuela and with all those engaged in rescue and relief operations. These earthquakes come at a time when millions of Venezuelans continue to face significant humanitarian needs. The European Union is in contact with the authorities and stands ready to support emergency response efforts while already working with partners to assess urgent humanitarian needs as more information becomes available.

chunks.title: Venezuela: Deadly earthquake will deepen suffering
chunks.text: ## Venezuela: Deadly earthquake will deepen suffering Statement by Jan Egeland, the Norwegian Refugee Council’s (NRC) Secretary General following the 7.2 and 7.5 magnitude earthquakes in Venezuela: “What NRC aid workers witness on the ground in and around Caracas is devastation beyond belief in the wake of the major earthquakes that had their epicentre West of Venezuela’s capital. The deadly earthquake struck in the evening of a national holiday, when many families were at home. The NRC office building in Caracas sustained damage, but thankfully all our staff are safe and accounted for. “This earthquake will deepen the suffering for millions already in dire need.

chunks.title: Venezuela: Deadly earthquake will deepen suffering
chunks.text: The NRC office building in Caracas sustained damage, but thankfully all our staff are safe and accounted for. “This earthquake will deepen the suffering for millions already in dire need. More than a quarter of the country’s population needed urgent aid even before the earthquakes. “NRC has been working in Venezuela for more than two decades and will provide emergency relief to the countless families that have lost their homes and property and have seen loved one perish in the rubble. We are currently assessing the most urgent needs and will seek funding from donor nations and the private sector to scale up our support for those most severely stricken.

chunks.title: Venezuela: Deadly earthquake will deepen suffering
chunks.text: “NRC has been working in Venezuela for more than two decades and will provide emergency relief to the countless families that have lost their homes and property and have seen loved one perish in the rubble. We are currently assessing the most urgent needs and will seek funding from donor nations and the private sector to scale up our support for those most severely stricken. “The deep suffering of the crisis-engulfed people in Venezuela has been neglected for too long. For the last three years aid workers on the ground have received less than a third of the funding needed for providing even the minimum of humanitarian relief needed. Donors must urgently step up support as this earthquake has become a catastrophe on top of a crisis.

chunks.title: Venezuela: Deadly earthquake will deepen suffering
chunks.text: For the last three years aid workers on the ground have received less than a third of the funding needed for providing even the minimum of humanitarian relief needed. Donors must urgently step up support as this earthquake has become a catastrophe on top of a crisis. There can be no delay in this support. National authorities and the international community must step up their cooperation immediately to provide relief and enable a viable plan for much needed reconstruction.” **Notes to editors:** On the evening of 24 June, Venezuela was hit by two back-to-back earthquakes measuring 7.2 and 7.5 on the Richter scale. The epicentre of the earthquakes is close to the capital Caracas, which was seen significant damage including to NRC’s office.

chunks.title: Statement on Venezuela by Tom Fletcher, Under-Secretary-General for Humanitarian Affairs and Emergency Relief Coordinator, 25 June 2026
sources: UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs
chunks.text: *Geneva, 25 June 2026* We are fully mobilised to support the people of [Venezuela]( following the deadly and devastating earthquakes that hit the country yesterday. I’m in constant contact with our team in Caracas, led by Humanitarian Coordinator Gianluca Rampolla, to ensure a swift and effective response. He has spoken this morning to the interim President and we are assessing urgently what is needed. Our team in Venezuela is working with the authorities to identify priorities.

chunks.title: Statement on Venezuela by Tom Fletcher, Under-Secretary-General for Humanitarian Affairs and Emergency Relief Coordinator, 25 June 2026
sources: UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs
chunks.text: He has spoken this morning to the interim President and we are assessing urgently what is needed. Our team in Venezuela is working with the authorities to identify priorities. OCHA is coordinating the rapid deployment of Urban Search and Rescue Teams from across the international community through the International Search and Rescue Advisory Group. I am surging a rapid response team to reinforce the OCHA team in country. The solidarity and practical offers from the region and beyond are superb.

chunks.title: La Croix-Rouge intervient au Venezuela alors que les besoins augmentent à la suite de deux puissants séismes successifs
sources: International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies
chunks.text: **Caracas/Panama/Genève, le 25 juin 2026** — Deux puissants séismes ont frappé le centre-nord du Venezuela dans la soirée du 24 juin, à moins d'une minute d'intervalle : une première secousse de magnitude 7,2 s'est produite vers 18 h 04 (heure locale), suivie 39 secondes plus tard d'un séisme principal de magnitude 7,5. Les épicentres étaient situés dans la région de Yaracuy, selon l'Institut d'études géologiques des États-Unis (USGS). Les séismes ont provoqué l'effondrement de bâtiments et endommagé des habitations ainsi que des commerces à Caracas et dans plusieurs États du pays. Les dégâts les plus importants ont été signalés à La Guaira et dans le Grand Caracas.

chunks.title: La Croix-Rouge intervient au Venezuela alors que les besoins augmentent à la suite de deux puissants séismes successifs
sources: International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies
chunks.text: Les séismes ont provoqué l'effondrement de bâtiments et endommagé des habitations ainsi que des commerces à Caracas et dans plusieurs États du pays. Les dégâts les plus importants ont été signalés à La Guaira et dans le Grand Caracas. Les autorités nationales ont déclaré l'état d'urgence, suspendu les cours et les activités non essentielles, ordonné des évacuations préventives, lancé des opérations de recherche et de sauvetage et mis en place des centres d'accueil pour les personnes sinistrées, tandis que les hôpitaux prennent en charge les blessés. Les réseaux d'électricité, de télécommunications et de transport ont été perturbés. D'importants dommages ont également été signalés sur des infrastructures essentielles de santé et de transport, entraînant des interruptions ou un fonctionnement limité de certains services publics.

chunks.title: La Croix-Rouge intervient au Venezuela alors que les besoins augmentent à la suite de deux puissants séismes successifs
sources: International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies
chunks.text: Les réseaux d'électricité, de télécommunications et de transport ont été perturbés. D'importants dommages ont également été signalés sur des infrastructures essentielles de santé et de transport, entraînant des interruptions ou un fonctionnement limité de certains services publics. Les évaluations des dégâts restent préliminaires et l'ampleur réelle de l'impact humain n'est pas encore connue. De fortes répliques continuent de représenter un risque supplémentaire pour les communautés touchées ainsi que pour les équipes d'intervention. La Croix-Rouge vénézuélienne est pleinement mobilisée.

chunks.title: La Croix-Rouge intervient au Venezuela alors que les besoins augmentent à la suite de deux puissants séismes successifs
sources: International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies
chunks.text: De fortes répliques continuent de représenter un risque supplémentaire pour les communautés touchées ainsi que pour les équipes d'intervention. La Croix-Rouge vénézuélienne est pleinement mobilisée. Son réseau national d'hôpitaux et de polycliniques reste opérationnel et continue de fournir des soins. La Société nationale a déployé des équipes de secours pour soutenir les opérations d'évacuation et de recherche et a envoyé, durant la nuit, quatre équipes d'évaluation rapide dans les zones les plus touchées, tout en mobilisant les stocks de secours prépositionnés. Bien que son siège national ait subi d'importants dégâts, la Croix-Rouge vénézuélienne s'assure de la sécurité de son personnel et de ses volontaires, active ses protocoles de sécurité et diffuse des conseils de prévention face aux séismes auprès des communautés, alors même que nombre de ses volontaires interviennent tout en étant eux-mêmes touchés dans leurs quartiers.

Bien que son siège national ait subi d'importants dégâts, la Croix-Rouge vénézuélienne s'assure de la sécurité de son personnel et de ses volontaires, active ses protocoles de sécurité et diffuse des conseils de prévention face aux séismes auprès des communautés, alors même que nombre de ses volontaires interviennent tout en étant eux-mêmes touchés dans leurs quartiers. Alors que les évaluations se poursuivent, les besoins les plus urgents devraient concerner les opérations de recherche et de sauvetage, les abris d'urgence pour les familles dont les habitations ont été endommagées ou détruites, ainsi que les soins de santé d'urgence, notamment la prise en charge des traumatismes et le soutien psychosocial. L'accès à l'eau potable, aux services d'assainissement et aux articles ménagers essentiels devrait également constituer une priorité dans les prochaines heures et les prochains jours. Les communications étant perturbées et de nombreuses familles ayant été séparées, les Sociétés de la Croix-Rouge d'Équateur, de Colombie, du Mexique, du Costa Rica, du Honduras et d'Argentine — des pays qui accueillent d'importantes communautés vénézuéliennes — ont déjà activé leurs services de rétablissement des liens familiaux afin d'aider les personnes à retrouver des nouvelles de leurs proches.

chunks.title: IOM Spokesperson Statement on Venezuela Earthquakes
chunks.text: **Geneva, 25 June 2026** – The International Organization for Migration (IOM) is deeply saddened by the devastating earthquakes that have struck Venezuela, causing widespread destruction, numerous fatalities and injuries, and affecting countless families and communities. Our thoughts are with all those who have lost loved ones, been injured, or seen their homes and livelihoods destroyed. At this difficult moment, we stand in solidarity with the people of Venezuela as well as the first responders working tirelessly to save lives and assist those affected. Many people are displaced or in urgent need of assistance.

chunks.title: IOM Spokesperson Statement on Venezuela Earthquakes
chunks.text: At this difficult moment, we stand in solidarity with the people of Venezuela as well as the first responders working tirelessly to save lives and assist those affected. Many people are displaced or in urgent need of assistance. IOM teams are assessing the situation and coordinating closely with national and local authorities, UN partners, and humanitarian organizations to determine the most pressing needs and support a rapid response. As part of its preparedness efforts, IOM is gearing up to provide emergency shelter assistance, water, sanitation, hygiene, and health services as well as essential non-food items to affected families, while supporting efforts to ensure that displaced populations receive the protection and assistance they need. The scale of this disaster demands swift and collective action.

chunks.title: IOM Spokesperson Statement on Venezuela Earthquakes
chunks.text: As part of its preparedness efforts, IOM is gearing up to provide emergency shelter assistance, water, sanitation, hygiene, and health services as well as essential non-food items to affected families, while supporting efforts to ensure that displaced populations receive the protection and assistance they need. The scale of this disaster demands swift and collective action. Every hour counts in reaching those who have lost everything and helping communities begin the path to recovery. IOM calls on the international community to support humanitarian efforts and stand with the people of Venezuela as they confront the devastating consequences of this earthquake. IOM remains committed to working alongside partners to deliver life-saving assistance and support recovery efforts in the days and weeks ahead. *For more information, please visit [IOM’s Media Centre](

chunks.title: Déclaration du porte-parole de l’OIM sur les séismes au Venezuela
chunks.text: **Genève, 25 juin 2026** – L'Organisation internationale pour les migrations (OIM) est profondément attristée par les séismes dévastateurs qui ont frappé le Venezuela, causant des destructions massives, de nombreux décès et blessés, et affectant d'innombrables familles et communautés. Nos pensées vont à toutes les personnes qui ont perdu des proches, ont été blessées ou ont vu leurs foyers et leurs moyens de subsistance anéantis. En ce moment difficile, nous nous tenons aux côtés du peuple vénézuélien ainsi que des premiers intervenants qui œuvrent sans relâche pour sauver des vies et porter assistance aux personnes affectées. De nombreuses personnes ont été déplacées ou ont un besoin urgent d’assistance.

chunks.title: Déclaration du porte-parole de l’OIM sur les séismes au Venezuela
chunks.text: En ce moment difficile, nous nous tenons aux côtés du peuple vénézuélien ainsi que des premiers intervenants qui œuvrent sans relâche pour sauver des vies et porter assistance aux personnes affectées. De nombreuses personnes ont été déplacées ou ont un besoin urgent d’assistance. Les équipes de l’OIM évaluent la situation et coordonnent étroitement leurs actions avec les autorités nationales et locales, les partenaires des Nations Unies et les organisations humanitaires, afin de déterminer les besoins les plus pressants et d’appuyer une réponse rapide et coordonnée. Dans le cadre de ses efforts de préparation, l’OIM se prépare à fournir une assistance d’urgence en matière d’abris, d’eau, d’assainissement et d’hygiène, de services de santé, ainsi que des articles essentiels non alimentaires aux familles touchées, tout en veillant à ce que les populations déplacées bénéficient de protection et d’assistance. L’ampleur de cette catastrophe exige une action rapide et collective.
